papers.title: Causal Diffusion for Extreme Super-Resolution in Interactive Games
papers.abstract: Existing game super-resolution methods typically operate at moderate upscaling factors, struggling to recover fine visual details from extremely low-resolution inputs (e.g., 120p). At such resolutions, super-resolution shifts from reconstructing existing information toward synthesizing missing visual details. While video diffusion models offer powerful generative priors for this challenging task, their dependence on future frames limits their applicability to interactive games. We present CIDER, a causal diffusion framework for extreme game super-resolution that synthesizes high-frequency details from current and past low-resolution frames, guided by G-buffers (depth and motion vectors) to preserve scene structure and temporal consistency. We collect data from two AAA games (Cyberpunk 2077 and Black Myth: Wukong). To reduce inference load, we develop a lightweight latent projection encoder tailored to ultra-low-resolution inputs, fine-tune a decoder (TAE) on our high-resolution outputs, and distill the diffusion model to reach interactive frame rates. Our experiments demonstrate high-fidelity 8$\times$ upscaling from 120p to 960p at around 13 FPS, outperforming state-of-the-art game upscalers in visual quality and showing potential for 16$\times$ magnification.

papers.title: Stability of independence polynomials of well-covered Ferrers graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every root of the independence polynomial of a well-covered Ferrers graph lies in the open unit disk centered at $-1$, that is, $|x+1|<1$. Consequently, the polynomial is strictly stable. We also exhibit a general Ferrers graph whose independence polynomial is not stable.

papers.title: High-precision proper motions toward the Galactic bulge Baade's window from a decade of DECam observations
papers.abstract: A complete characterization of the Galactic bulge stellar populations could offer important clues on the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. However, most bulge fields are hampered by high stellar crowding, strong interstellar extinction, and by heavy contamination from foreground disk stars. We aim to derive proper motions (PMs) towards the Baade's window by using DECam observations, extending kinematic studies of the Galactic bulge below the turn-off to a much larger field of view. We combined three datasets observed with DECam in the $r$-band spanning a ${\sim}$ 10-year baseline. As a pilot study, we only analyzed the field covered by a single detector. We developed an astrometric calibration pipeline that corrects for the DECam tree-ring pattern and residual distortions, tying all positions to the Gaia DR3 reference frame, and used them to derive PMs. We isolated the bulge population through a strict cut in $μ_{\ell^\ast}$, refined with a Gaia DR3 parallax selection. We measured PMs for $48\,239$ stars in the pilot field, with a median uncertainty of $0.65$ mas yr$^{-1}$ at $r_0<18$ mag. Our PMs agree closely with Gaia DR3, and reaches ${\sim}1.5$ magnitudes deeper than Gaia and a comparable depth to VIRAC2 in terms of relative completeness. We found velocity dispersions along Galactic longitude and latitude of $σ_{μ_{\ell^\ast}}=2.76\pm0.03$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and $σ_{μ_b}=2.49\pm0.02$ mas yr$^{-1}$ for the Galactic bulge, consistent with HST studies. We estimated a foreground contamination of ${\sim}14\%$ before any kinematic selection. The cleaned color-magnitude diagram reaches below the main-sequence turnoff, and shows no evidence for a large population younger than ${\sim}4$-$5$ Gyr in this field. Moreover, since the LSST camera shares the same CCD technology as DECam, this work offers a valuable precursor for crowded-field astrometry in the Rubin era.

papers.title: Resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in one-dimensional quantum scattering
papers.abstract: We study resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in a one-dimensional quantum-scattering model. Two incoming electrons scatter independently from a symmetric double-barrier structure and the sector with one reflected and one transmitted electron is selected. The idealised delta-function barriers used in earlier work are replaced by exponentially localised cusp barriers, $U(x)=U_0\exp(-|x\mp d/2|/a)$, for which the single-barrier scattering problem is exactly solvable in terms of modified Bessel functions of imaginary order. We derive the corresponding reflection and transmission amplitudes, verify their current normalisation and validate them independently by direct numerical integration. Two separated cusp barriers are then combined through a Fabry-Pérot composition, whose accuracy is quantified by solving the full two-centre Schrödinger equation. In the well-separated regime the approximation reproduces the full resonance positions to high accuracy. The concurrence zeros are controlled by the resonance phase condition $δ(κ)+κd=nπ$, with a continuously unwrapped single-barrier reflection phase $δ$. We also calculate the post-selection probability $P_{RT}$, showing explicitly that large conditional concurrence can occur in a low-probability sector. Systematic scans in barrier width, integrated strength and reference momentum show that finite width can shift off-resonant concurrence maxima and, depending on the reference momentum, reduce their attainable height. The results identify resonance-controlled conditional entanglement as a robust feature of the well-separated double-barrier geometry rather than an artefact of the zero-range idealisation.

papers.title: High-Sensitivity Magnetometry with Scalable Mixed SQUID Arrays
papers.abstract: The utilisation of Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUIDs), a loop of superconducting material hosting two Josephson junctions, has long been at the forefront of quantum sensing. To enhance performance and signal power, modern architectures connect multiple SQUIDs into two-dimensional series-parallel arrays called Superconducting Quantum Interference Filters (SQIFs). A major recent advancement, called a mixed-SQUID array, integrates junction-free ``bare" loops alongside active SQUID loops, offering a promising strategy to engineer high-performance alternatives to traditional SQIF technology. However, a rigorous theoretical optimization and performance scaling analysis for this novel geometry remains lacking. In this work, an analytical framework, validated against full numerical simulations, is developed to establish fundamental design rules for this technology. This work systematically examines how key quantum sensing parameters evolve as a function of loop inductance, parasitic coupling, and overall array dimensions. Crucially, it is demonstrated that these mixed SQUID arrays circumvent the severe inductive screening losses inherent to conventional SQIF designs, achieving a performance boost in flux sensitivity in the range of $2-4\:\times$ under realistic device parameters.

papers.title: A Novel Dataset and Framework for Schenkerian Optical Music Recognition
papers.abstract: Music theory enables performers, composers, and listeners to engage more deeply with music. Schenkerian analysis (SchA) is a particularly illustrative and widely used approach for modeling tonal structure, organizing music into hierarchical layers of harmonic and voice-leading relationships. Despite its importance in pedagogy and scholarship, producing well-formatted Schenkerian graphs remains difficult. A typical workflow might involve writing the Schenkerian analysis on paper, and then manually, painstakingly, entering each symbol by hand into music software, exporting to vector graphics, and manually refining layouts in graphical editors. Existing optical music recognition (OMR) systems for handwritten common western music notation (CWMN) can be leveraged for their ability to recognize small-scale symbols common to those in SchA. However, CWMN OMR models generally fail to recognize large symbols such as phrase slurs, struggle with dense notation, and do not recognize Schenkerian analysis markings. Thus, these models do not extend well to digitizing SchA. This paper introduces a novel framework for optical music recognition of both CWMN and SchA. Our novel contributions include (1) an ensemble model in which each individual model follows a different image-cropping scheme for improved object detection, (2) a topological neural network architecture for notation assembly, where candidate hyperedges attend to one another and perform hierarchical message passing, (3) the first dataset of labeled handwritten SchAs, gathered with novel model integration to the OMR-annotation software, MuNG Studio, and (4) the first algorithm for converting semantic Schenkerian graphs into typeset format.

papers.title: Tracking and Limiting Unsupported Claim Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Provenance-Aware Framework
papers.abstract: This research examines how unsupported claims change as they move through multi-agent pipelines. It also examines whether preserving provenance can reduce these changes. We test both homogeneous and heterogeneous pipelines. Homogeneous pipelines use the same model across agents, while heterogeneous pipelines use different models. We compare the baseline with a provenance-aware framework. The framework passes each claim with its support status, source, evidence and transmission history. No new evidence is introduced during transmission. We measure changes in claim meaning, unsupported detail accretion, semantic drift, and provenance preservation. These metrics show whether the framework limits unsupported changes as claims pass between agents.

papers.title: Strong numerical radius orthogonality on bounded linear operators
papers.abstract: Orthogonality is an important tool for studying bounded linear operators. In this paper, we introduce the concept of strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators and then, discuss the properties about numerical radius orthogonality, strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators as well as relationship between them.

papers.title: A generalized Bayesian method for identifying local and global changepoints in dynamic network data
papers.abstract: We introduce a generalized Bayesian approach to multiple changepoint analysis in dynamic network data based on a multinomial log loss function and a prior distribution that imposes low-rank structure and sparsity on the model parameters. The method can detect local and global changes in network structure by incorporating information from both the full adjacency matrices and network summary statistics. Moreover, the proposed method is agnostic to the true data-generating process. From the generalized posterior distribution, we can make simultaneous inferences with meaningful uncertainty quantification about the locations of changepoints as well as deduce the network attributes and summary statistics that characterize them. For posterior simulation, we develop an efficient Gibbs sampler based on Pólya-Gamma data augmentation with a computational cost that grows linearly with the number of observed edges in the dynamic network. Simulations across several benchmark network models show that the proposed method is often more accurate and flexible than competitors. We demonstrate the practical value of the method through applications to an email communication network and an international conflict network.

papers.title: Learning Video Foresight Reasoning from Unlabeled Videos via On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Video foresight reasoning requires vision-language models to anticipate future events or next actions from currently observed videos. Existing methods fit future captions, rationales, or full visual states, but face two limitations. First, they rely on annotations or external large models for supervision, limiting scalability. We address this with an on-policy self-distillation framework that turns past-future video pairs into a natural self-supervised signal without extra annotations or LLM supervision. Second, they treat the whole future clip as equally valuable, although most of it is irrelevant context information. We address this by defining a foresight score, from which we obtain a contrastive privilege advantage that drives the model to learn the most valuable future information. Since the score is intractable, we optimize a tractable lower-bound surrogate that interpolates this advantage, computed between the true and a random reference future, with a teacher-student distillation advantage; together, they amplify decision-relevant content information and suppress irrelevant context information. We call the resulting framework Future-OPSD. On open-ended prediction and closed-ended planning, Future-OPSD improves base models by up to 14.2 and 15.9 points without compromising general video understanding. Code will be available at https://jingchensun.github.io/future-opsd/

papers.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on weighted Catalan numbers
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on when the 2-adic valuations of weighted Catalan numbers equal those of Catalan numbers.

papers.title: A High-Resolution Stellar Extinction Map of M31 from PHAT and PHAST Photometry
papers.abstract: High-resolution extinction maps of resolved external galaxies, such as M31, are crucial not only for accurately correcting dust extinction and reddening toward individual sources within the galaxy, but also for characterizing the distribution and evolution of interstellar dust in external galactic environments. We aim to construct a high-resolution and large-coverage stellar-traced extinction map of M31, based on multi-band photometric data from the HST PHAT and PHAST surveys. Using a stellar template library built from the PARSEC stellar evolution models and adopting the average extinction law of M31, we apply a matching method analogous to the SPar algorithm to derive A_V values for approximately 65 million stars. The extinction map is then generated using a HEALPix adaptive-resolution scheme. The resulting map covers approximately two-thirds of the star-forming disk of M31, with a maximum spatial resolution of 1.61 arcsec. The median extinction across the map is A_V = 1.24 mag. Comparison with previously published stellar- and dust-emission-based extinction maps shows broadly similar large-scale morphology, while differences remain in the extinction values. The extinction map further reveals fine-scale features such as inter-arm filaments, supernova-driven cavities, and spur-like structures. The map has been publicly released through the NADC platform and is expected to serve as an important observational basis for extinction correction in subsequent astronomical observations and for related M31 scientific studies.

papers.title: Verification of Statistical Properties: Redefining the Possible
papers.abstract: We revisit the setting of Interactive Proof Systems for Distribution Testing, introduced by Chiesa and Gur (2018), showing that a simple twist on the task requirements may lead to dramatic improvements, allowing verifiers with constant sample complexity. We define and investigate the multi-prover and zero-knowledge versions of these interactive proof systems, using as flagship example the task of farness verification - the "dual" version of closeness testing. We hope our results will inspire others to investigate and analyze the power and limitations of multiple provers for distribution verification.

papers.title: Mechanistic Analysis of Unified Proximity-Tactile Observation by a Capacitive Fingertip Array Constrained by a Metal Phalanx
papers.abstract: A capacitive fingertip array on a metal phalanx under thin silicone skin senses centimetre-scale conductive targets by fringing fields and contact force by dielectric compression. Electrode-to-body parasitics exceed the useful proximity increment by one to three orders of magnitude, and crosstalk and time-division-multiplexing (TDM) settling prevent identifying the capacitance-to-digital converter (CDC) reading with the electrode-target capacitance. The array is modelled as a multi-conductor system (sensing electrodes, driven-shield nodes, phalanx ground and an external target). The CDC measurand follows from the Maxwell capacitance matrix, with each inactive termination in the observation operator. Three mechanisms are examined: driven-shield hiding of shield-branch current and gain/phase-mismatch leakage; distinct far- and near-field operators; and TDM settling as a frame-rate limit set by shield load. A single layer used for both proximity and force reads Delta C = Delta C_force + Delta C_dielectric(epsilon_target), so its force map cannot be material-independent. A dual-array stack is analysed: the outer array is grounded as a Faraday screen during contact, and the inner array reads silicone-gap compression. FEM simulations give a monotonic, nonlinear contact response (4.6 fF at 0.05 mm to 370 fF at 0.5 mm on a 1.08 pF base), a nylon-versus-metal difference of at most 0.3 fF at exported-matrix resolution (not mesh-converged), mutual-term cancellation under driven-shield readout, and about 1 fF crosstalk on the coarse mesh. In proximity mode, electrode-shield coupling of 1.47 pF makes 10^{-3}-10^{-4} mismatch a quantitative gate: a 15.9 fF increment at 5 mm equals the leakage at |epsilon_A| ~ 10^{-2}. Force map, mechanical crosstalk and all bench quantities remain unvalidated; the equations and FEM evidence are a baseline for prototype calibration, not measured performance claims.

papers.title: Serial Dependence Emerges from Optimizing Vision for Noise Robustness
papers.abstract: Human visual perception is dynamically shaped by the recent past, a phenomenon known as serial dependence. Mechanistic models show that a residual memory trace can generate this dependency, yet its functional purpose (why the visual system should carry information forward in time at all) remains debated. We tested the hypothesis that serial dependence emerges as a normative consequence of optimizing vision for robustness against sensory noise. We trained recurrent autoencoders (a CNN encoder, a ConvGRU memory module, and a CNN decoder) to reconstruct natural videos corrupted by Gaussian noise, with no objective referring to perceptual history. Models that used their temporal memory achieved lower reconstruction error than memory-free counterparts, and this advantage widened as training noise increased, indicating that integrating past context is an adaptive denoising strategy. Probing the trained models with Gabor and dot sequences, we found that memory gave rise to serial dependence spontaneously: an attractive bias toward previous orientations and a spatial "continuity field" toward recently seen locations, both strengthening with training noise. Across temporal delays, the model's serial dependence was strongest for the immediately preceding stimulus and decayed monotonically. This profile quantitatively matched human orientation judgments, including an independent public dataset, once a known response-autocorrelation confound was controlled: an apparent non-monotonicity in one dataset reflected this measurement artifact rather than a genuine model-human mismatch. These findings suggest that serial dependence need not be an idiosyncratic quirk but can arise as a byproduct of optimizing for noise robustness, offering a normative account of perceptual history-dependence that complements existing mechanistic explanations and links behavior to an underlying computational objective.

papers.title: Bottlenecked: The Capital Cost of Protected DeFi Lending
papers.abstract: Securing hundreds of billions of dollars in decentralized finance (DeFi) requires both cryptographically secured collateral and economic capital to absorb losses that collateral alone cannot cover. Composability makes both the amount and location of this protection matter: Kelp's nearly \$300 million April 2026 bridge exploit showed how an attacker could borrow against stolen assets across lending markets. We study how to allocate junior capital that absorbs losses before users incur losses in lending protocols. The main object we study is a tripartite graph that records user assets, their covered liabilities, and the junior capital permitted to pay them. Cuts in this graph determine what protection is missing, while a static security game on the graph defines how much such protection should cost. We call this cost the adversarial default premium (ADP), which can be viewed as the excess cost of insurance in composable financial systems. We then study the joint cost of funding loans and protecting their creditors via this insurance. In a tripartite graph with $N$ borrowers and $M$ lenders, we show that existing systems such as Aave and Morpho have an insurance cost that is $Θ(N)$. Under mild assumptions, we show that the optimal graph has an insurance cost that is $Θ(\sqrt{N})$ with small constants. We apply our model to numerous 2026 DeFi cyber attacks and estimate ADP and the performance of optimized graphs. We find practical capital cost savings of up to 34.5% for our optimized design versus designs that resemble Aave and Morpho. Our results suggest that new lending protocols can improve capital efficiency by treating junior capital as a first-class constraint in protocol design.

papers.title: Tensor products of additive groups as reciprocity sheaves
papers.abstract: We compute the Nisnevich reciprocity sheaves associated with tensor products of the cube-invariant objects for the additive and multiplicative groups, with at least one additive factor. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, these sheaves decompose into direct sums of absolute K$ä$hler differential sheaves with binomial multiplicities. As an application, we compute the associated reciprocity sheaves of the Hochschild homology of the additive object.

papers.title: A Stochastic Tamed-Regularized Random Batch Method for Uncertain Particle Systems with Singularities
papers.abstract: The coefficients of particle systems often exhibit uncertainties due to incomplete knowledge. For particle systems with uncertainties and singularities in the drift and diffusion terms, existing methods may encounter numerical blow-up. In this paper, we propose a novel stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) method for such uncertain particle systems with singularities. Specifically, since singularities in the diffusion term are more challenging than those in the drift term, building on a tamed scheme, we design an exponential regularization strategy that more effectively mitigates singularities in the diffusion term. This strategy ensures that the stochastic Galerkin (sG) projection coefficients remain finite even when the corresponding integrals for the original singular diffusion coefficient diverge. The sG method is applied to handle the random coefficients, and a random batch approach is then employed to reduce the computational complexity of large-scale simulations. Several theoretical properties of the proposed algorithm are established. Numerical tests demonstrate that the str-RB algorithm exhibits weak convergence, achieves lower errors than major existing methods across singular tests, and remains stable in a wider range of singular regimes. This work provides a robust and accurate approach for uncertain particle systems with singularities, laying a foundation for high-performance solvers in uncertain many-body dynamics.

papers.title: Spectral Estimation with Deformed Decompression
papers.abstract: Sample covariance matrices are fundamental objects in machine learning and statistics, with valuable information encoded into their eigenvalues. When treating modern problems, the scale of these matrices can become prohibitive for tractable computation. This creates a critical need for "spectral decompression": a method for inferring the eigenspectrum of a very large-scale model using only information from its smaller realizations. Existing methods fall into two main categories: those relying on spectral inversion; and those that rely on Free Decompression techniques. On the one hand, spectral inversion is a fundamentally ill-posed problem that is notoriously unstable, often failing to yield reliable results in finite-size settings. On the other hand, while Free Decompression was recently proposed to address this scaling, its reliance on the Nica-Speicher framework restricts its use to unitarily invariant ensembles, a symmetry condition that subsampled covariance matrices fail to satisfy. In this work, we introduce Deformed Decompression (DD), a novel framework for the stable, forward-extrapolation of spectral densities. By leveraging properties of the companion matrix, DD recasts the spectral decompression problem as a directed evolution of the Stieltjes transform of the companion matrix. This approach bypasses the instabilities of traditional inversion and provides a robust methodology for scaling covariance matrices and even their generalized variants (including Hessian matrices) that lack unitary invariance. We demonstrate the utility of our framework through experiments on a variety of random matrix examples, showing that DD successfully captures the complex spectral signatures of large-scale systems.

papers.title: Analysis of Multi-Client Inference Techniques for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) are a new class of machine learning model for generalizable robot control. While they enable robots to perform complex tasks in unseen environments, serving VLAs leaves hardware idle between inference passes and under-utilized during inference. Serving multiple clients at once can improve utilization, but fundamental multi-client techniques such as batching and co-execution have not been characterized for VLAs. We therefore characterize the trade-offs these known techniques impose across latency, throughput, power, and hardware utilization. Our findings inform trade-offs and challenges for future multi-VLA serving systems.

papers.title: An Infinite Family of Overpartition Congruences Modulo 1944
papers.abstract: Let $\overline p(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$. We prove that $\overline p(16^α(96n+76))\equiv0\pmod{1944}$ for all nonnegative integers $α$ and $n$, extending the congruence for $\overline p(96n+76)$ established by Smoot. The key step is a three-term congruence modulo $243$ relating $\overline p(m)$, $\overline p(16m)$, and $\overline p(256m)$ for $m\equiv4\pmod6$. We derive this relation and the two initial congruences using theta-function dissections. A separate theta-series argument establishes divisibility by $8$.

papers.title: CodeReviewBench: An Automated Benchmark for Evaluating the Software Factory
papers.abstract: As AI agents ship more code with minimal human oversight, code review becomes the critical quality-control checkpoint -- but one without a reliable, objective verifier: review quality is nuanced and ultimately a judgment call by the PR author. Existing benchmarks are structurally misaligned with this: annotators are third-party reviewers, like the bots they evaluate, not the PR authors who actually decide what to fix. They also rely on small, static issue sets that require full re-evaluation as tools update, limiting how frequently progress can be tracked. We introduce CodeReviewBench, built on a fundamentally different signal: revealed developer preferences -- if a developer acts on a bot's suggestion, we treat it as useful; if they ignore it, we do not. This signal is mined daily from the public GitHub event stream, yielding 500K+ judged PRs across 18 tools, and refreshes continuously as tools evolve. We validate the developer preference against an independent offline benchmark: the two agree on precision rankings and independently detect the same product updates within days of vendor releases. Together, these form the benchmark.

papers.title: Extracting Next Generation Access Control Policies from Natural Language Using LLMs: An Intermediate-Representation Approach with Back-Translation Verification
papers.abstract: Organizations write access-control rules in natural language, but NIST's Next Generation Access Control (NGAC) needs them as a formal policy graph. Large language models (LLMs) can automate this translation, but their output can break the format, add rules the text does not state, or drop conditions. We present NGAC-IR, which follows model-driven engineering (MDE). First, the LLM fills in an intermediate representation (IR), a JSON template that records who may, must or must not do what, on which resource and under which condition; a grammar keeps the output within this template. Second, a compiler that uses no LLM converts the IR into an NGAC policy graph and links each rule to its source sentence. Third, a back-translation check writes each rule in English and asks an LLM whether the source sentence states it. On four public datasets, all outputs could be compiled, compared with 95.5% without the grammar, and 95.7% were faithful to their sentence. NGAC-IR outperforms two published methods on all four datasets: the LLM-based Code4Policy in exact match and faithfulness, and the rule-based extractor of Abdelgawad et al. in rule type. The back-translation check sent 10.5% of sentences to human review and found 26 of the 31 errors. To test enforcement, we deployed the compiled policies in NIST's Policy Machine: they gave the expected decision for all 390 access requests, and the tested obligations were carried out. On one local server with open-weight models, all 714 sentences take about 20 minutes and 0.35 kWh, at zero API cost.

papers.title: CENTRY: A Probabilistic Latent-State Model for Continual AI Risk Estimation, Monitoring, and Regulation
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, yet existing AI safety frameworks primarily define, categorize, or govern AI risk rather than proposing implementable models and methods for continually estimating, monitoring, and regulating risk throughout an AI system's operational lifetime. This paper proposes CENTRY, a probabilistic framework that enables continual risk estimation, monitoring, and regulation of a deployed AI system from its interactions with its environment. The framework models AI risk as arising from three intrinsic sources: datasets, hardware resources, and models/algorithms. A structured latent-variable model is developed in which the latent representation is decomposed into a fast interaction subspace that captures the evolving AI--environment dynamics and three slow latent subspaces that encode the long-term risk states associated with the dataset, hardware, and model components. Rather than requiring a ground-truth risk label at every time step, the component-risk states are treated as latent variables and are learned by maximizing a variational evidence lower bound, optionally informed during training and continual refinement by evidence-supported behavior--cause records. The resulting framework unifies continual probabilistic inference, online risk estimation, and adaptive risk regulation in an implementable architecture. Under the explicit assumptions stated for the corresponding results, we establish formal guarantees spanning safety, learning, inference, and operations, including finite-horizon and asymptotic risk-budget compliance, regret and convergence bounds for adaptive regulation, consistency and identifiability of component-risk ratings, and detection-delay, false-alarm, containment, and computational-complexity characterizations.

papers.title: Acceleration of Sparse and Irregular Workloads through Energy-Efficient Stream Extensions
papers.abstract: The slowdown of Moore's law and Dennard scaling has motivated computer architects to uphold performance scaling through architectural specialization. So far, most efforts have focused on highly regular workloads, which exhibit good data locality, ample reuse, and a data-independent execution flow. As this specialization hits diminishing returns, attention shifts towards sparse and irregular workloads, which are essential to applications like sparse neural networks, multiphysics simulations, and graph analytics. However, they lack the convenient properties of highly regular compute that modern architectures are optimized for, resulting in very low (<10%) functional unit utilization on traditional CPUs and GPUs. The most promising approaches to their general hardware acceleration leverage memory streams, which decouple data movement from execution. In this thesis, we explore energy-efficient hardware stream extensions that significantly accelerate sparse and irregular workloads in general-purpose systems without specializing to specific application domains or compromising on regular-workload performance. We design a flexible, core-coupled stream extension supporting affine and indirect streams as well as intersection and union of sparse tensors. We integrate it into an energy-efficient RISC-V compute cluster, achieving significant performance and energy efficiency benefits on general sparse linear algebra, and further use it to accelerate stencil computations, spiking neural network inference, and model-predictive control. We evaluate it at scale in a 432-core 2.5D RISC-V system fabricated in 12nm FinFET, achieving leading compute utilization and energy efficiency on sparse and irregular workloads while remaining competitive on regular workloads. Finally, we extend chip-level interconnects with end-to-end irregular streams, improving performance, energy efficiency, and bus utilization.

papers.title: MG-EDA: Maturity-Gated Skew-Normal Estimation of Distribution Algorithms
papers.abstract: Gaussian estimation of distribution algorithms shrink their variance on slopes and stall far from the optimum. This paper equips the corrections that act along the direction of movement -- a mean shift, an elongation of the covariance along the path and a skewness -- with the rule they lack: a calibrated gate, driven by a maturity statistic of the population, decides whether, how strongly and for how long each correction acts, and when the gate is closed the algorithm is exactly the estimation of multivariate normal algorithm (EMNA). The statistic is a cumulative path of whitened mean shifts with an inverse-Wishart correction, whose expectation is one under a null model without systematic movement and whose quantiles give thresholds with known false-alarm rate. It gates the three corrections as three rank-one terms of one matrix sampling equation, the skewness being carried by a skew-normal sampler that preserves the estimated mean and covariance; all vanish at maturity. We call the resulting algorithm the maturity-gated EDA (MG-EDA). A full factorial study on a training set of black-box optimization benchmarking (BBOB) functions separates the parameters: variance scaling is the prerequisite, the mean shift needs a feedback correction removing the injected shift from the statistic, the elongation turns the variance loss on a slope into a gain, and the skewness substitutes for the mean shift rather than complementing it. On held-out instances MG-EDA with the first- and second-order corrections is significantly better than the skewness-only predecessor and than EMNA with variance scaling, ties with EMNA with anticipated mean shift, and trails the adapted maximum-likelihood Gaussian model (AMaLGaM) in 20 dimensions.

papers.title: Looking Right Is Not Being Right: Evaluating the Geometry of Agent-Built 3D Scenes
papers.abstract: Vision-language agents can reconstruct rooms from video as editable 3D scenes, but convincing renders do not establish geometric accuracy. We introduce a scan-referenced evaluation and use controlled experiments to study reconstruction accuracy, the role of geometric inputs, and agents' ability to verify and correct their scenes. Our geometric score measures surface, depth, and furniture placement agreement with laser scans of 30 real rooms on a 0-100 scale. The strongest tested agent, GPT-6 Astra, scores 51.4 from video alone, while a dense reconstruction from the same video scores 75.9. Given the point cloud used for that reconstruction, Astra produces an editable scene that scores within three points of it. Agents also inherit input errors: rescaling the supplied geometry changes scene scale almost proportionally. During revision, viewing renders improves appearance more consistently than geometry. Logs of their tool calls show that agents repeatedly measure their inputs but rarely compare them with the scenes they build. To provide this missing check, we introduce a geometric error report that compares each saved scene with the agent's input points and lists the largest discrepancies. Without new geometric evidence, the report raises the revision gains of GPT-6.1 Terra and Sol by 3.9 and 5.5 points over concurrent controls.

papers.title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can infer private information from shared images, including locations, personally identifiable information (PII), and personal attributes such as age and sex, even from medical images. Adversarial perturbations can protect such information against black-box VLMs, but existing methods overlook image quality and introduce visible artifacts into the images they protect. We present SecretAgent, the first general multi-agent framework that protects image privacy against VLMs while preserving visual fidelity. LLM agents iteratively locate the visual evidence that reveals private information and adapt an invisible perturbation to the target VLM's answers and to an appearance reviewer agent, which rejects any candidate with visible artifacts. We instantiate SecretAgent with two complementary variants: SecretAgent-Gradient optimizes the perturbation through six surrogate encoders for cross-model transferability, and the gradient-free SecretAgent-Tool composes procedural noise and achieves the best perceptual fidelity on three of the five datasets. Experiments on four privacy applications (geolocation, PII, facial, and medical) across five datasets and six VLMs show that SecretAgent preserves image quality substantially better than existing methods while achieving state-of-the-art privacy protection in every application, and that its protection transfers to other VLMs.

papers.title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
papers.abstract: How much information relevant to predicting the future of a passage (i.e. predictive information) is carried by the preceding text, and how is this information distributed along that history? These questions are fundamental to understanding both the statistical structure of language and what large language models (LLMs) can learn about it. Indeed, LLMs trained to predict the next token in text must exploit this predictive information, so its organization determines how the structure of language becomes available to the model to learn. We develop a theory for the organization of predictive information based on the scaling behavior of a family of information measures, and the theory predicts that if this organization has the same form at all measured length scales -- i.e., it has a self-similar structure -- then the information measures evaluated at different lengths collapse onto a common form. We observe this scaling collapse in long text documents, showing that predictive information is present at every length scale we measure and has a self-similar structure. Self-similarity is a considerably stronger property than showing the existence of long-range dependencies, and it constrains the process generating the text. More broadly, our results give quantitative support to the empirical observation that conditioning on more distant text continues to reveal new structure in language to LLMs.

papers.title: On generation of the coefficient field of a primitive HMF by a single Fourier coefficient: An application of Nekovář's Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a non-CM primitive Hilbert modular form (HMF) over a totally real number field, of parallel even weight $k\geq 2$, with coefficient field $E_f$, and let $F_f \subseteq E_f$ denote the field fixed by the inner twists of $f$. In this article, we establish an analogue of Ribet's large image theorem for the residual Galois representations associated with $f$, by applying Nekovář's large image theorem (cf.~\cite[Theorem B.5.2]{Nek12}) to the automorphic representation $π(f)$ associated with $f$. As a result, we prove that if $f$ has no nontrivial inner twists, then $E_f$ is generated by a single prime Fourier coefficient, for a set of prime ideals of Dirichlet density one. We derive this result as a consequence of a more general theorem established for $F_f$.

papers.title: Tokenize Moments, Not Frames: Tokenizer-Aware Budget Allocation for Training-Free Video LLM Acceleration
papers.abstract: Video large language models (LLMs) represent each video with thousands of visual tokens, and training-free accelerators that prune or merge these tokens lose accuracy on long videos. Analyzing frame similarity and the vision tokenizers of 16 open models, we trace this loss to a step before token selection. Under a token budget, the frames of a long video are sampled farther apart than the roughly 2 s over which frames remain similar. The two-frame 3D patches of models such as Qwen-VL then blend two unrelated scenes into each visual token, a double exposure that arises before any pruning or merging. Fixed-size tokenizers such as InternVL's avoid this blend but respond differently to the same reduction. We propose ESSENCE, a training-free method that tokenizes moments, segments within which frames remain similar, rather than frames. Before encoding, a closed-form rule uses the sampling interval and the tokenizer class to set the number of token grids and the dimension to reduce; visual tokens are then released from later LLM layers. Against five recent accelerators on Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3.5, ESSENCE achieves higher accuracy in 58 of 60 comparisons at matched mean time to first token (TTFT). With 80% of the tokens, it matches the average accuracy of the full Qwen models at $1.6\times$ faster TTFT; on GLM-4.1V, it exceeds the full model by up to 3.4 points. Code is available at: https://github.com/zhkandsrz/ESSENCE.

papers.title: Parametric excitation of nano-scale spin waves with controlled phase by an open-resonator-type transducer
papers.abstract: Parametric excitation is one of the most effective methods for the excitation of nano-scale spin waves (SW) (or magnons) in magnetic films and nano-waveguides, as this method removes restrictions on the excited wave wavelength imposed by a finite width of the excitation transducer. Especially efficient parametric excitation of SW is achieved if the SW excitation is based on the effect of voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA). However, in a traditional parametric excitation process, the excited propagating waves have an arbitrary phase, which prevents the use of such waves in signal processing applications. Here, we demonstrate that the use of an VCMA transducer in the form of an open resonator with controlled partial reflections of waves at the boundaries allows one to excite SW having only two allowed phase states, controlled by the phase of the parametric pumping and reflections at the transducer boundaries. These reflections, also, lead to a reduced value of the parametric excitation threshold. In addition, micromagnetic simulations reveal the possibility to tune the phase distribution of the excited magnons using static voltage, which could be useful for applications in probabilistic computing.

papers.title: Improving the Optimisation Landscape for Particle Mixtures
papers.abstract: Several methods in statistics and machine learning represent a predictive distribution as an equally weighted mixture of models, or particles, trained via the mixture predictive likelihood. However, we prove that the mixture predictive likelihood is poorly suited to gradient-based optimisation, because it does not identify how the mixture is decomposed across particles, so that a poorly matched particle can be starved of training signal. As a remedy, we study a convex combination between the individual risk, i.e. the average log loss of the individual particles, and the mixture risk. At the particle level, this regularised risk imposes a reverse-KL barrier on the responsibilities of the particles, so that no particle can be starved of training signal. These phenomena are illustrated in two case studies: In the first, a predictively-oriented posterior is computed using mean-field Langevin dynamics, and the numerics are well-behaved only when our regularisation is employed. In the second, ensembles of low-rank adapters are jointly fine-tuned on large language models, across four backbones and eight multiple-choice reasoning benchmarks; direct minimisation of the mixture risk leads to responsibility starvation, whose severity decreases as the competence of the backbone increases, whereas our regularised estimator attains a lower held-out mixture risk on every backbone considered.

papers.title: Semigroup Hessian Estimates for Underdamped Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract:
For the semigroup $e^{t\mathcal L}$ of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we bound the Hessian $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ when $
abla f$ is uniformly bounded. When the potential is strongly convex outside a ball and has bounded second and third derivatives, and the damping rate is above an explicit threshold, the bounds on $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ decay exponentially in time with constants free of the dimension. The proof combines the Wasserstein contraction of the dynamics with a Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for the degenerate noise. As an application, we prove the uniform-in-time error of the stochastic gradient UBU integrator, with an explicit coefficient of the numerical bias in the step size, proportional to the covariance of the stochastic gradient noise.

papers.title: Large Reported CHB-MIT Adaptation Gains Disappear with Pretrained Encoders and Matched Probes
papers.abstract: Dani and Liebe (2026) (DL) report that adapting the final encoder block of BIOT and CBraMod with self-supervised learning (SSL) improves CHB-MIT seizure-detection ROC-AUC by 36.2 and 29.5 points over linear probing. We investigate these results with their released code and an independent pipeline. The release loads pretrained weights for adaptation only when an otherwise unset configuration key is supplied, and its CBraMod probe reads the reconstruction head with dropout active. With pretrained initialisation and a probe on the encoder output in evaluation mode, the fixed-recipe adaptation gain on DL's split is -0.6 points for BIOT (95% interval [-3.8, +2.6]) and +0.01 for CBraMod ([-0.02, +0.04]) across five seeds. Across DL's split and five subject rotations on CHB-MIT and Siena Scalp EEG, with equally tuned linear probes (30 configurations, up to 500 epochs, validation-based early stopping), mean adaptation effects range from -1.1 to +5.7 ROC-AUC points over 18 comparisons (related settings and feature variants). Twelve of 18 support equivalence within +/-3 points under dependence-adjusted inference (8 of 12 rotation and 4 of 6 fixed-split comparisons); six are unresolved. After correcting rotation intervals for dependence, no positive effect has a 95% interval excluding zero. The +/-3 margin is an analysis threshold, not a clinically validated one, and smaller margins support fewer equivalences. Two fixed-probe gains near +21 points shrink under the same tuning, with smaller benefits unresolved. We also audit a CHB-MIT protocol shared by at least 14 papers. No tested configuration reproduces DL Table 1 as a whole. These findings concern the tested configurations; the encoder-level probe and subsequent checks were chosen post hoc.

papers.title: Galvanometer Mirror Based Femtosecond-Laser Volumetric Displays
papers.abstract: Femtosecond-laser-induced plasma enables self-emissive voxels to be generated directly in air for drawing three-dimensional images. Galvanometer-mirror-based beam scanning provides a method for rapidly moving plasma voxels using a relatively simple optical configuration. However, the generated plasma voxels are not ideal points but luminous regions with finite lengths and widths. Variations in voxel shape and orientation caused by focusing and scanning conditions may therefore affect the appearance of rendered points and lines. Nevertheless, quantitative relationships between focusing and scanning conditions and plasma-voxel geometry remain insufficiently characterized in systems using a two-axis galvanometer mirror and a single focusing lens. Here, we quantitatively investigate how focal length and two-axis galvanometer scan angle affect the shape of plasma voxels and the projected inclination of their principal axes. For focal lengths ranging from 75 to 300 mm, the mean plasma length increased from 1.39 to 4.64 mm. These results indicate that increasing the focal length produces more elongated and anisotropic plasma voxels. The projected inclination of the plasma principal axis varied approximately linearly with the corresponding scan angle, although the response differed between the two scanning axes. These results provide quantitative design data for selecting focusing conditions and correcting voxel shape and orientation according to scanning conditions in galvanometer-mirror-based aerial volumetric displays.

papers.title: Uncovering Multimorbidity Patterns Through a Novel Randomized Clustering Algorithm
papers.abstract: Patients with several chronic conditions rarely share the same combination: in four years of the nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), we find 32,789 distinct combinations of two to seven conditions, and over 90% of those involving four or more occur in a single patient. Methods that search for common combinations discard most of this heterogeneity. We present the Randomized Length Sequential Clustering Algorithm (RLSCA), which links diseases by lift, a pairwise association measure counted only above a user-set support threshold. A mixed-integer program repeatedly selects and removes the group of conditions with the greatest internal lift, up to a random size; 100 iterations yield a database of clusters scored by size, rediscovery frequency, and body systems spanned. In MEPS 2019, stratified by age and sex, RLSCA recovers known groupings at a high threshold, such as diabetes with lipid disorders and hypertension, and at a lower threshold returns clusters of up to eight conditions spanning five body systems. Frequent itemset mining, at its lowest feasible support, finds no set above five conditions; hierarchical clustering cannot control cluster size. With a clinical large language model, the database could suggest which further conditions a patient is at risk of.

papers.title: Topology-only Local Network Alignment, Part 2. DijSLA: Stochastic Greedy Extension for Cross-Species GO Annotation Prediction
papers.abstract: Sequence similarity has long been a strong signal for protein function prediction, whereas the predictive value of network topology has been difficult to verify. Since a protein's function is largely defined by its interaction partners, and since similar interactions are expected across species, aligning protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks by topology alone should uncover functionally related proteins. Topology-only global network alignment has recently produced high-quality functional predictions, but it has yet to be shown that local regions of topological similarity can do the same. We introduce DijSLA (Dijkstra-inspired Stochastic Local Alignment), the first local network alignment algorithm designed from the ground up to use only topology. We adopt a seed-and-extend strategy: starting from seed pairs of proteins with similar network topology, we expand the alignment in a Dijkstra-inspired manner, following edges out of the aligned set to node pairs with near-maximal similarity. Rather than expanding deterministically, we inject randomness so that we can sample many high-quality alignments, in which node pairs with robust topological similarity "rise above" the noise and reveal functional similarity. Using networks and GO annotations from April 2010, we predict annotations validated against those from April 2020. With Network Alignment Frequency (NAF), a robustness measure that correlates with prediction precision, we make predictions with precision on par with or better than the best sequence-based methods and broadly similar to that of global topological alignment. Compared with existing local aligners, DijSLA produces larger, topologically high-quality alignments, which yield dramatically more predictions with higher validation rates, while using less CPU time and far less memory. Code is available at https://github.com/waynebhayes/BLANT/tree/master/CDijkstra.

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Key Distribution Hardware Across Operating Conditions
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is entering national fibre networks, but published secret key rates (SKRs) are measured over different distances, wavelengths, classical traffic loads and clock rates, so systems are hard to compare. We write the SKR as the product of the transmitter clock rate, the channel transmittance and the secret key per received pulse. This third factor, the noise-normalised key rate (NNKR), needs four commonly reported parameters and depends mainly on the equipment wherever the SKR is proportional to transmittance. A companion metric, the implementation efficiency (IE), compares the SKR with the ideal key rate of its channel, including classical-traffic noise. For fixed loss-limited equipment, NNKR is independent of channel loss, whereas the fraction of the repeaterless bound varies 1.6-fold over 2-25 dB. An analytic model relates the flat loss range of NNKR to the detector noise count rate and dead time. We apply both metrics to ten published coexistence experiments, and NNKR to 42,115 measurements from four systems of two vendors and four high-rate laboratory systems. For one production system, NNKR has a 6.9% coefficient of variation over 17 dB of attenuation and agrees within 0.7 dB with three of four published deployments of that platform. Under coexistence, that platform's NNKR and IE stay within 0.5 dB of their standalone values. In decibels, NNKR is a sum of component penalties, as in an optical link budget, and for one laboratory system the budget from its published parameters and measured secure fraction closes within 0.3 dB.

papers.title: Joint SLA Admission and Risk Allocation for Cloud Resource Provisioning
papers.abstract: Cloud controllers must reserve enough CPU and memory to meet demand without leaving too much capacity idle. Under a shared service-level agreement (SLA), a shortage of CPU or memory (considered as resource) counts toward the same limit. Dividing the allowed shortage risk between them changes how much extra capacity each need. We study this choice when forecast-error histories are short or correlated over time. Our controller compares different approaches to split the allowed shortage risk between resources. For each split, the controller uses historical forecast errors to determine how much extra capacity to reserve. It checks whether the history is enough to support that split and its consistency across different parts of the history. Among the splits that pass, it chooses the one with the lowest combined cost of shortages and idle capacity. Otherwise, the controller continues serving the workload with a calibrated fallback. In our simulation, we set a joint SLA target of sufficient CPU and memory in at least 95% of time slots and used 192 hours of historical forecast errors to structure the controller. Compared with always using fallback, the controller reduced the time slots allocation with either of the resource shortage by 1.04 percentage points on average. This reduction came with a 0.0091 increase in normalized cost from shortages and idle capacity. In the Bitbrains trace, five nonoverlapping test windows did not provide clear evidence of whether shortages increased or decreased. We also examine how execution delays and adjustment limits affect this trade off.

papers.title: The Illusion of Evaluation: Challenges in Agentic Product Evaluation Practice
papers.abstract: Agentic products introduce risks that extend beyond those of their underlying models, arising from their tools, permissions, data access, safeguards, and operating conditions. Existing evaluation instruments provide useful evidence about model behavior and agents in defined harnesses, but their results do not necessarily transfer to deployed products or cover risks created by product configurations and interactions. Identifying and measuring such risks is especially difficult before deployment, when failure pathways, exposure, and outcome distributions may be poorly understood. This raises a fundamental question: what can evaluation evidence establish about the safety of a particular product, and what decisions can it legitimately support? We call the illusion of evaluation the appearance of safety assurance when producing an evaluation result is treated as sufficient evidence for claims that extend beyond what was measured. Drawing on practitioner experience, prior research, and twelve illustrative product contexts, we identify six methodological challenges spanning product-risk identification, ecological and measurement validity, metric interpretation, outcome verification, evidence transfer, and evidentiary sufficiency. We propose a granular transparency-and-decision-relevance record that makes risks, system configurations, assumptions, uncertainty, and evidentiary limits explicit. The proposal is a reporting and reasoning aid, not proof of safety or a deployment-approval standard. We conclude with open questions on valid product-level measurements, evidence transfer, and decision sufficiency.

papers.title: Categorification of the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebras of polygons
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ be the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebra of a polygon with $m$ boundary punctures ($m\geq 3$). Building on the quantum cluster algebra structure of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ established by Cao and the authors, and on the monoidal category $\mathcal{C}(Δ^{m-2})$ of finite-dimensional modules over the quantum affine algebra $U_q'(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n)$ introduced by Kashiwara, Kim, Oh and Park, where $Δ$ is the Garside element of ${\rm Br}_n$, we give a monoidal categorification of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$. As a consequence, $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ has a basis with positive structure constants. A key role is played by the subalgebra $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ spanned by the stated $n$-webs whose $m-1$ edge weights are zero. We show that $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ is a quantum cluster algebra whose seed coincides with the Kashiwara--Kim--Oh--Park seed of $Δ^{m-2}$. Hence it is the quantum Grothendieck ring of a monoidal localization, at the frozen modules, of a subcategory of $\mathcal{C}(Δ^{m-2})$ with the same simple objects, and a quantization of the braid variety $X(Δ^{m-1})$. The whole algebra $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ is a skew Laurent extension of $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ in $(m-1)(n-1)$ frozen variables.

papers.title: Leader Finding: A New Variation of Expert Finding in Community Question Answering
papers.abstract: Expert finding ranks people by their knowledge of a given topic. Many job positions need more than topical expertise, and a team leader is a clear case. A suitable leader knows the technical areas of the project without being overqualified, has strong managerial knowledge, and communicates well with the team. We study the leader finding problem, where the query is a project and a team and the output is a ranked list of candidate leaders. We model the problem in a probabilistic framework that combines technical fit, managerial knowledge, and communication with the team, and we propose one evaluation metric for each of these qualities. On two large collections built from Stack Overflow, the best configuration of our model more than doubles the NDCG@10 of the strongest baseline. These results show that a ranking of leaders must balance several qualities that topical expertise alone does not capture.

papers.title: Partially canonical axes in large language model representations
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) develop rich internal representations of language, but whether their individual coordinate axes carry meaning, or whether meaning is encoded only in directions in representation space, is still an open question. A common assumption is that individual axes in LLMs are arbitrary. We here challenge this view: across 12 LLMs from six model families, the native axes are reliably more aligned with other models' representations, with human brain responses to language, and with interpretable linguistic features than randomly rotated axes that preserve the same geometry. The native axes nonetheless fall well short of the best achievable alignment, so LLM coordinates are not fully arbitrary but also not fully canonical: they are partially canonical. A theory of how LLMs represent language must explain both the population geometry they learn and why individual units acquire patterns of response profiles that recur across systems.

papers.title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval
papers.abstract: Production retrieval systems are tied to the embedding model that indexed their corpus. Moving queries to a different encoder normally requires re-embedding the whole corpus, and at cold start there are no query logs while every document embedded by the new encoder incurs an API or compute cost. We present ERA (Embed, Route, Adapt), a system for cold-start cross-model latent retrieval. ERA spends a small anchor budget on maximally informative documents, selected from the existing target index via Cosine Farthest Point Sampling, trains a lightweight adapter with a Manifold Alignment Loss that couples directional alignment with orthogonal regularization to prevent representation collapse, and pairs the adapter with a deterministic router that escalates the rare, hard queries that define perceived retrieval quality. Across five BEIR datasets, ERA matches or outperforms point-wise L2 and embedding-conversion baselines, with relative gains of up to 35% nDCG@10 on Arguana, and on clustered corpora its anchor selection also improves prior methods under a fixed anchor budget. With 1.2 ms of adapter and router overhead on top of a ~20 ms local encoder, ERA at a 20% nominal escalation budget reduces end-to-end query latency from roughly 160 ms to 38-86 ms while concentrating escalations on the queries where the projection fails most.

papers.title: Broad-line ambiguity in IC 1495
papers.abstract: Published analyses disagree on whether the 2004 6dFGS spectrum of IC 1495, a barred Seyfert galaxy in the 2MIG isolated-galaxy catalogue, contains broad H-alpha. We compare it with a 2024 SDSS-V/BOSS spectrum to assess changes in broad-line visibility. In 2024, the [O III] profile favours a blueshifted wing with intrinsic FWHM ~640 km/s, while [S II] and [O I] favour single-component fits. Among six H-alpha+[N II] models with free narrow-line kinematics, the BIC-preferred fit includes broad H-alpha with intrinsic FWHM ~2000 km/s. However, adding broad H-alpha worsens the BIC when H-alpha and [N II] share two narrow kinematic components. Broad H-alpha is not detected in the 2004 spectrum under the adopted criterion. Injection-recovery simulations of a reference broad component (FWHM ~1930 km/s; broad-to-narrow H-alpha flux ratio 0.82) yield recovery fractions of 27-35% in baseline simulations and 11-55% across the grid. At 1.5 times this flux ratio, baseline recovery rises to 42-55%. Aperture and flux-calibration uncertainties limit absolute line-flux comparisons. Narrow-line excitation, Chandra spectroscopy (intrinsic N_H ~2.3 x 10^23 cm^-2 in the fiducial model), and long-term optical and mid-infrared variability support an absorbed, variable Seyfert nucleus. The model-dependent 2024 broad-H-alpha candidate and limited 2004 sensitivity do not establish a change in broad-line visibility between the epochs.

papers.title: What Does the Visual Encoder Buy? Visual Information Gain in Encoder-Free Multimodal Pretraining
papers.abstract: Recent scaling studies ask whether vision-language models still need a visual encoder by comparing encoder-free and encoder-based models on the next-token loss of the text in image-text data. This loss can fall without any use of the image, and two runs with the same loss can differ in what they take from it. Visual information gain (VIG) is the loss increase when the image is replaced by a uniform one. It splits exactly into global information, carried by image statistics, and layout information, which shuffling the patches within the image destroys. We apply it to decoders with 158M to 1.04B parameters that read pixel patches through a linear embedding, evaluated every billion tokens up to 40B, and to 19 public checkpoints. In our decoders the image lowers the loss by 3% to 46%, depending on the image type. Global information is present after the first billion tokens. Layout information starts near zero, grows slowly with training and does not grow with model size on five of six image types, and a larger batch reaches the same loss with less of it. With a frozen SigLIP 2 encoder in front of the same decoder the loss is lower only when the arrangement of the image is intact. On shuffled images the losses with and without the encoder agree to within 0.04 nats on five of six image types, so the net advantage of the encoder in the loss is layout information, above all the ability to read text in images. Public encoder-free models at production scale (Gemma 4 12B, NEO, Mono-InternVL) do acquire layout information. On the same documents they have 0.53 to 0.76 nats of it, against 0.65 to 0.82 for recent encoder-based models and 0.04 to 0.07 for our decoders, and their released training stages show it rising. These results agree with the reported parity of the two families when both are trained from scratch and place the reported advantage of a pretrained encoder in layout information.

papers.title: RoboCap-10k: A Metrically Accurate Egocentric Dataset for Robot Learning
papers.abstract: Egocentric video is the most scalable source of manipulation data for robot learning, but its difficulty lies in producing high-quality supervision. Existing large corpora lack metric 3D labels or rely on heterogeneous devices, motion-capture labs, or a headset's built-in real-time tracker, whose accuracy is not reported for the released data. We introduce RoboCap-10k: 10,000 curated hours of unscripted manipulation recorded during workers' paid shifts in 11 countries, spanning 18 task families, 200 task types, and 2,000 tasks. Every hour is captured on one device, the RoboCap, a 250 g hat with six synchronized global-shutter cameras and dual IMUs. Online calibration brings every device below 1 px of epipolar error, visual-inertial SLAM yields gravity-aligned 6-DoF head trajectories, and a multi-view hand tracker yields metric cm-precise hand poses. Each episode is annotated with task and sub-task language captions. Project page: https://robocap10k.com

papers.title: Spatially multiplexed opto-electronic Ising machine with single-shot parallel readout of 100,000 spins
papers.abstract: Ising machines offer a promising route to solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems by mapping them onto the ground state of the Ising model. Free-space optical implementations are attractive for their inherent parallelism, scalability, and energy efficiency, yet nearly all rely on individual, sequential spin updates, leaving most of this parallelism unexploited. Here, we reclaim it with a free-space optical analog Ising machine built from off-the-shelf components in which every spin is addressed in parallel and read out in a single camera shot, while letting the system evolve under analog dynamics rather than being written and read one spin at a time. We demonstrate this architecture with over 100,000 spins, the largest spatially multiplexed analog Ising machine reported to date, with a realistic path beyond one million spins limited only by spatial-light-modulator and camera resolution. Across sparse and dense MaxCut and fully connected number-partitioning instances, our machine matches state-of-the-art solution quality. Because every spin updates in parallel, throughput increases with system size, unlike time-multiplexed machines, which slow as problems grow. The same free-space geometry also lets us solve more than 50 problem instances simultaneously, further boosting throughput. Together, these results mark an important step towards a scalable, and energy-efficient Ising machine.

papers.title: Multi-Tier Edge Triage: Optimizing Latency for Safe Clinical Agents
papers.abstract: Deploying generative AI agents in enterprise clinical workflows requires enforcing multi-dimensional safety and compliance policies--preventing HIPAA Protected Health Information (PHI) exposure, maintaining clinical scope-of-practice boundaries, ensuring patient-appropriate reading comprehension, and preserving brand integrity--under interactive latency constraints. Synchronous outbound calls to cloud Large Language Model (LLM) judges add substantial network and decoding overhead onto the critical response path. We present Multi-Tier Edge Triage, a safety screening architecture that co-locates a compact Tier-1 sequence classifier on the clinical agent's host server, resolving clear queries in-process without a network round-trip and escalating only ambiguous queries to a Tier-2 cloud LLM judge. To evaluate Tier-1 encoders without length or unigram shortcuts, we construct four length-matched contrastive twin benchmarks seeded from MedSafetyBench, ASQ-PHI, and a synthetic four-mandate clinical assistant policy (Generic HealthCorp). While frozen local encoders match cloud models on structured PHI detection (>= 98.3% accuracy in <= 23.5 ms), they degrade markedly on semantic safety and symmetric-blocklist prompts. However, end-to-end representation fine-tuning closes the multi-policy accuracy gap: a fine-tuned 335M-parameter BGE-Large classifier achieves 98.90% out-of-fold accuracy versus 99.20% for a zero-shot cloud LLM judge (exact McNemar p = 0.648, zero shared errors), 97.8%-98.2% recall, and a 0.0%-0.4% over-refusal rate in 39.0 ms (>14x faster than cloud LLM evaluation on our benchmark host). Per-policy error analysis reveals ceiling local recall on PHI (100.0%), brand (100.0%), and clinical scope (98.7%-99.3%) violations, isolating residual errors to reading-level checks (93.3%-95.3%) and motivating targeted multi-tier escalation.

papers.title: Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs
papers.abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides a noninvasive view of functional interactions across the brain, which can be represented as connectivity graphs for neurological disease analysis. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being paired with such representations, yet it remains unclear whether they genuinely reason over the underlying connectivity or simply respond to surface-level cues that may trigger learned priors. We probe this question through a controlled study of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnosis from resting-state functional connectivity, isolating one factor at a time to determine what drives an LLM's predictions on brain connectivity graphs. Across six models, from small open-weight LLMs to a proprietary one, the same pattern holds: the results provide little evidence that predictions are consistently grounded in subject-specific connectivity. Brain region names, numeric formatting, and prompt framing shift what a model predicts without improving how well it separates ADHD subjects from Controls; perturbing the graph changes predictions no more for clinically meaningful regions than for random ones; and the models' own justifications contradict the values they cite, inconsistently interpreting the connectivity evidence provided to them. Across every probe, predictions follow the model's built-in class bias and the surface form of the prompt rather than the subject's connectivity, calling into question a premise underlying current LLM brain integration work. Our code is available at https://github.com/Roy025/ADHD-code.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
papers.abstract: The growing complexity of electronic systems demands efficient design flows, yet EDA scripting remains a bottleneck: proprietary APIs are sparsely documented, and errors often appear as silent failures or cryptic exceptions. Hand-crafted knowledge helps but is difficult to maintain as toolchains evolve. We present ZhuLong-SE (Self-Evolution), an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces. Building on ZhuLong, it enhances the task-level harness with API retrieval, documentation responses, isolated sandbox execution, and static checking, then adds governed cross-task self-evolution. Beyond solving individual tasks, ZhuLong-SE distills past execution traces into a three-tier memory store governed by ground-truth anchoring, disconfirmation filtering, held-out rollback, and anti-leakage retrieval. On the 158-task EDA-Eval-PyAether benchmark, the full task-level harness, with self-evolution disabled, achieves 92.4% pass@1 and outperforms ZhuLong on all five tested LLM backbones. On a harder instance-disjoint test set, self-evolution from the bare configuration surpasses a human-crafted-experience baseline by 2.5 percentage points (80.0% vs. 77.5% pass@1).

papers.title: InfantConnect: integrating developmental brain atlases and electrophysiological network analysis
papers.abstract: The brains of infants change considerably during the first two years. Hence, developmental neuroimaging requires computational tools that account for age-related anatomy while supporting the analysis of electrophysiological data. For instance, cortical surfaces, electrode montages, tractography atlases, and electroencephalography (EEG) analysis utilities are commonly distributed across separate resources and software environments. Here we propose an open Python framework that brings these components into a shared three-dimensional workspace and supplements interactive visualization with command-line tools for EEG quality control, preprocessing, source-related visualization, and effective-connectivity analysis. The command line version can also be invoked by a model context protocol server to be used by artificial intelligence agents. The tool supports age-indexed cortical surfaces, infant scalp and skull templates, electrode locations, tractography, sensor-level connectomes, and directed estimates based on Granger causality and transfer entropy. We demonstrate the resource using representative anatomical visualizations and evaluate the effective-connectivity workflow on controlled toy networks with explicitly specified nodes and directed interactions. These tests provide targeted evidence about the connectivity workflow rather than a general validation of causal inference from clinical EEG. Performance benchmarks on low resolution electromagnetic tomography and validation of effective connectivity are provided.

papers.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
papers.abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. Self-improvement in an embodied world cannot be read from one measure. Existing benchmarks measure task progress, world-knowledge question answering (QA), and episodic memory, but a correct answer does not show that the agent ever observed the evidence for it, and progress does not show what the agent learned. We introduce AstronautBench, which measures one agent's self-improvement through three views on the same run: what it knows, whether its own evidence supports that knowledge, and how far it gets in the world. It is built on the game Outer Wilds, where each episode is a 22-minute loop after which the world resets, only the agent's knowledge carries over, and progress is gated by knowledge. After every episode, we measure the places reached and ship-log rumor facts revealed, the correctness of answers to 164 questions about the world, and whether each answer is supported by the frames and position the agent cites from its own recorded play. Two LLM judges from different model families check every answer. In eight-episode baselines with GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon planners, which act through a learned controller or their own gamepad inputs, the three views do not move together, so any one of them alone gives an incomplete picture of whether the agent is improving. The GPT-6.1 Sol agent's correct answers grow from 14.6% to 26.8% of all questions, but at episode 8 only 59 to 68% of them are supported by its cited evidence. It reveals no new rumor facts after episode 3, while the places it reaches and its memory keep growing. More than half of the answers that become correct after episode 3 cite only evidence from earlier episodes.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming
papers.abstract: Pit-stop strategy in Formula 1 is a sequential decision problem under uncertainty, in which strategists decide at each lap whether to pit and which tire compound to fit. We develop a data-driven simulator, calibrated with historical race data, that captures tire degradation, drivers' recent performance, overtaking, yellow flag events, and rivals' pit-stop decisions. We train agents with five Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms and compare them with a Quadratic Mixed-Integer Programming (QMIP) formulation that is optimal in deterministic single-driver settings. Without uncertainty or competition, all DRL methods except TRPO achieve near-optimal performance. With a full grid of competitors and stochastic race events, the ranking of DRL methods depends on the evaluation setting: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and its recurrent variant are the only methods that improve on the QMIP both in fully simulated races and when the actual 2024 races are replayed. Averaged over eight circuits, PPO improves on the QMIP by 0.33 and 0.49 positions in the two settings and Recurrent PPO by less, and in the replay PPO finishes 0.66 positions ahead of the drivers' actual strategies simulated in the same races. The QMIP performs similarly to the other methods, even though it cannot anticipate yellow flag events.
