Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert. We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and $π_{0.5}$ in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.

papers.title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities
papers.abstract: Each fibre-reinforced composite structure has a unique material architecture. The manufacturing methods used and the presence of defects lead to local variations which require material-scale models that can resolve the response in real time at every location in the structure. Concurrent multi-scale schemes provide this capability, but at a prohibitive computational cost for large structures as the number of integration points and time increments scales with size. Surrogates have been studied extensively as replacements for material-scale models to mitigate these computational limitations. A surrogate must represent an arbitrary local architecture including defects, track the irreversible material state over an unknown number of increments, remain stable when driven recursively by its own predictions, and fit within the memory available at every integration point. Here, a Composites World Model based on a Multi-Modal Spiking Transformer architecture is designed to meet these requirements. The proposed architecture combines a material encoder, a Spiking Neural Network memory block that tracks the long-term internal state of the material, and transformer blocks that learn the short-term applied strain state. The system is trained in three stages: material architecture encoding, base training on short time windows, and recursive fine-tuning with scheduled sampling to suppress cumulative error drift. The trained model is disassembled at inference and coupled to a non-linear FE solver, enabling structural scale simulation of composites containing embedded defects. Benchmarks against experimental results for IM7/8552 laminates under tension, compression and transverse shear, for pristine and wrinkled composites, show that the SNN memory block successfully tracks the material internal state and results in prediction errors between 0.4% and 4.8%.

papers.title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
papers.abstract: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface. In both cases the reactor is observed by a small flux monitor detector near the source, while JUNO measures the antineutrino flux at two baselines, suppressing correlated flux and detector systematics. Using the measured Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and its covariance, we model a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) core for the microreactor and a low-enriched uranium (LEU) core for the surface unit, and discuss various potential sources of systematic uncertainties and their impact on the precision of $\thone$. The underground microreactor could improve on JUNO's reach by a factor of three to four, to $\relsth \simeq 4\%$ over a decade, while the surface reactor would reach the present global-fit precision, $\relsth=2.5\%$, in about three years, provided the emission rate is monitored across reactor relocations to the sub-percent level.

papers.title: Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs
papers.abstract: We quantify how thermal resummation affects electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave predictions in classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. We compare multi-field partial dressing (PD), which retains the full thermal functions and determines scalar masses and mixing from gap equations, with the Parwani and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) prescriptions at identical zero-temperature inputs. Completed first-order transitions dominate the conformal scan under all three prescriptions. PD typically gives the strongest and most supercooled transitions, reaching $T_p/T_c \simeq 0.5$ versus $T_p/T_c \gtrsim 0.8$ for Parwani and AE. At every conformal point where all three predict completion, PD gives the largest gravitational-wave peak amplitude, followed by Parwani and AE. The non-conformal model has no universal ordering, and the prescription changes the type of thermal history across extended regions of parameter space. For representative benchmarks, PD and AE differ by up to about nine orders of magnitude in peak amplitude and a factor of about fifty in peak frequency. In multi-field PD, the dressed tadpole is not a gradient, so the reconstructed potential depends on the integration path. In benchmark tests, changing the path shifts the transition temperatures by at most about 7% and the peak amplitude by up to a factor of about three. This intrinsic ambiguity is smaller than the largest differences between prescriptions. Thermal resummation is a major source of uncertainty in these phase-transition and gravitational-wave predictions.

papers.title: Peanut/X-shaped bulges: Returning to the vertical resonance and separatrix
papers.abstract: We investigate the vertical structure and evolution of an $N$-body galactic bar by analyzing pure resonant orbits that form the skeleton of boxy/peanut/X-shaped (BP/X) bulges in Cartesian and action-angle spaces ($θ_\text{res} = θ_z - θ_R, \, J_z$). We show that the main backbone of this skeleton is made up of separatrix orbits associated with unstable figure-of-eight resonant orbits. For the first time, we examine the long-term behavior of the separatrix, showing how it sinks to the bottom of phase space and shrinks. As a result, ``fresh'' orbits involved in a flat bar are captured into vertical resonance, passing through it near the separatrix and creating orbital crowding. This crowding traces the thickest part of the BP/X bulge and outlines the ends of its X-structure rays. The rise of orbits leads to changes in the potential and geometry of phase space in these regions. Over time, when the rise ceases, evolution slows and stops.

papers.title: Half-strings across the deconfinement transition of a $U(1)$ quantum link model
papers.abstract: The phenomenon of confinement is arguably the key feature of gauge theories regularly studied in high-energy and condensed matter physics. This causes hadrons to exist as stable particles in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) as bound states of quarks (and gluons), and strings in pure gauge theories. The promise of realizing such strings in quantum simulator setups have fueled extensive studies of a plethora of simpler lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Quantum link models (QLMs) generalize Wilsonian LGTs and yield richer scenarios of confinement. For example, the string joining two static charges in the spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ $U(1)$ QLM fractionalize, giving rise to confining phases that break the point group and internal symmetries spontaneously. It was further shown in PRL 130, 071901 (2023) that adding annealed $Q = \pm 2$ charges to this model qualitatively changes the confinement-deconfinement transition. In this paper, we examine the finite temperature phase transition both in the presence and the absence of annealed charges through detailed extraction of critical temperature, $T_c$ , and exponents. The (effective) string tension $σ$ at zero and finite- temperatures are compared between the theory with and without annealed charges. The quantity $T_c/\sqrtσ$ for the QLM with annealed charges is similar to the usual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory, while the theory without the charges provides a new universal value.

papers.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
papers.abstract: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves effective navigation with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain. Rather than teaching the brain to predict geometric goals, we equip it with a semantic tool-calling interface for conveying movement decisions to an action expert in natural language. We first adapt the action expert to carry out these movement requests, then jointly improve the brain's movement decisions and the action expert's continuous execution through closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL). Trained on the same navigation episodes, ZeroVLN substantially outperforms representative SFT-based hierarchical VLN methods on standard VLN-CE (continuous environments) benchmarks, while inducing only minor changes to the brain's weights and largely preserving its general capabilities. To our knowledge, ZeroVLN is the first slow-fast VLN framework with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain, and the first to jointly optimize its slow and fast policies through closed-loop agentic RL in VLN-CE.

papers.title: Sequential Anytime Valid Tests for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment
papers.abstract: Inference-time alignment methods, such as Best-of-N (BoN), improve language model outputs by generating multiple candidates per prompt and selecting among them using a reward model. Much of this cost is wasted: a fixed budget is applied to every prompt, although the computation required by prompts varies widely. Adaptive methods halt once sampled answers appear settled, but their thresholds are tuned heuristics with no statistical control over early-stopping errors. We instead seek an anytime-valid stopping rule that takes an error tolerance $α$ as input and halts only once an answer is certified to hold a majority ($θ_a > 1/2$) under the generator's distribution. We aggregate candidates by final answer with a reward-weighted self-consistency (RWSC) score and treat stopping as a sequential test over the resulting clusters. Applying Wald's sequential probability ratio test to these clusters yields SPRT-RWSC, which performs well empirically, but its guarantee fails because the leading answer shifts during sampling, and the run is continuously monitored. Our main contribution, e-RWSC, replaces Wald's test with a betting supermartingale (an e-process) for every answer the policy produces, bounding the probability of ever certifying a non-dominant answer by $α$, uniformly over time and across all answers. The RWSC scores drive the bets, so they affect only how quickly a dominant answer $a^\star$ is certified, not validity; certification takes $O(\log(1/α)/d_{\mathrm{KL}}(θ_{a^\star}\|1/2))$ samples. Experiments across several language models, datasets, and reward models confirm the predicted $1/d_{\mathrm{KL}}$ scaling of cost and show that accuracy improves over baselines at substantially lower token cost.

papers.title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods
papers.abstract: The transition from fossil fuels presents significant challenges in energy management. To ensure a sustainable energy future, it is crucial to reduce energy consumption when possible and to synchronize electricity consumption and storage with the production from sources with low greenhouse gas emissions. This thesis explores a variety of energy management methods used to manage batteries, heat pumps, and other energy-related systems. The thesis presents three simulation cases alongside one real-world experiment to compare energy management done through simple rules, optimization, and machine learning methods. Furthermore, this thesis introduces TreeC, a novel machine learning-based method that learns understandable yet efficient energy management strategies, applicable to many cases. The three key contributions of this thesis can be summarized as follows: 1) The developed TreeC method demonstrates competitive performance compared to a variety of energy management approaches, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning, across a diverse set of energy management problems. The understandability of TreeC's energy management strategies greatly improves the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning-based energy management. 2) The real-world experiment highlights the need to validate energy management methods on actual hardware and not solely on simulations. Both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse than in simulations, due to, respectively, insufficiently representative training data and the real-time input data not being reliable enough. 3) Energy management algorithms reduce costs in electrified Belgian dwellings, particularly in poorly insulated dwellings, electric vehicle chargers, and photovoltaic installations. However, on average, these cost savings do not yet outweigh the current costs and effort required to implement such algorithms.

papers.title: Low-Latency Alerts of Massive Black Hole Binaries in LISA
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) for days to months before merger, offering opportunities for advance electromagnetic follow-up. To enable such observations, inference methods must provide rapid, continuously updated, and statistically calibrated posterior estimates, while remaining robust to overlapping sources. We present TRUFFLE (Time-evolving Rapid Updates For Follow-up of LISA Events), a simulation-based inference method for MBHBs in LISA data designed to meet these requirements. Our approach uses two networks, selected according to the time to coalescence relative to the end of the analysis window, $Δt_c$. An early-warning network, operating at $Δt_c \in [4~\mathrm{h}, 2~\mathrm{d}]$, estimates the chirp mass, mass ratio, and coalescence time to support electromagnetic follow-up scheduling. A near-merger network, operating at $Δt_c \in [-1~\mathrm{h}, +4~\mathrm{h}]$, infers nine parameters, including the sky position needed for telescope pointing. Both networks process the most recent six days of data using multiband time- and frequency-domain representations, which are summarized by a transformer to condition a normalizing flow. The networks are trained on the full orbit-driven LISA response and amortized over a 30-day range of observation epochs. The near-merger posterior can be corrected through likelihood-based importance sampling, with neural inference taking seconds and likelihood reweighting approximately five minutes on a single GPU. We obtain unbiased posteriors in the presence of overlapping sources, including plunging extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, resolvable Galactic binaries, and additional MBHBs merging up to two hours before the primary merger.

papers.title: Statistical Inference with Ill-Conditioned Random Weight Neural Network Sieves
papers.abstract: Random weight neural networks (RWNNs) are shallow networks whose hidden-layer parameters are randomly generated and then kept fixed, while only the output coefficients are estimated. Conditional on the sampled parameters, RWNN regression is a linear sieve problem with random approximation space. We show that such random sieves cannot remain uniformly well-conditioned as their dimension grows. For parametrized feature families satisfying polynomial covering and Lipschitz conditions, the eigenvalues of the population covariance matrix are proven to have polynomial upper bounds determined by the covering geometry of the parameter space, leading to a vanishing smallest eigenvalue. We develop approximation, estimation, and inference theory that explicitly treats the ill-conditioning. Under a $β$-Hölder source condition, we obtain both faster-than-Monte-Carlo $L^2$ approximation rates and new $L^\infty$ approximation bounds based on stratified sampling. We then derive improved consistency guarantees for ridge-regularized least squares driven by ridge effective dimension, spectral, and leverage-based stability conditions. For inference, we establish asymptotic linearity and Gaussian limits for linear functional directions while allowing the smallest eigenvalue of the population covariance matrix to vanish. Nondegeneracy is directional: we characterize it with a ridge-normalized Rayleigh quotient and extend it to smooth functionals via Riesz representation. Consistency of ridge-adjusted variance estimators is proved, yielding feasible studentized inference. Numerical experiments illustrate the deterioration of random-feature conditioning and the finite-sample behavior of the resulting estimation and inference procedures.

papers.title: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce \textbf{WeMM-Video}, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL. Evaluated across more than 120 benchmarks, WeMM-Video demonstrates superior performance in omni-modal video understanding and reasoning, while maintaining highly competitive capabilities across general audio, silent video, image, and text tasks. Specifically, in omni-modal video evaluations, our flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B establishes a new open-source state of the art, substantially outperforming proprietary models such as Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash and Seed2.0-Mini-0428 while narrowing the gap with the strong Gemini-3.0-Flash, and our compact WeMM-Video-9B surpasses the larger open-source Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct. We publicly release the WeMM-Video family along with our evaluation and reproduction pipeline to foster further research and development in the open-source community.

papers.title: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
papers.abstract: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. However, it is unknown how dedicated training of these networks can contribute to the successes of weight-space programming. We present a benchmark of LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, in which five LLMs edit convolutional networks and vision transformers on relabeling and error-correction tasks on Waterbirds, CIFAR-100, PACS and Entity-30. We report more than 2,600 such edit processes, whereby each edit is scored on held-out images for success, side effects and accuracy loss. We compare standard training with label smoothing, gradient-based editable training, and our Edit-Ready Training (ERT), a novel method that rehearses the direct, closed-form weight edits LLMs perform. We show that preparing networks for editing raises the success of LLM edits substantially where standard networks are hard to edit. ERT further achieves the highest mean score for GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 across all evaluated baselines. We will release our LLM testing framework alongside all tasks, editing trajectories and scores. Project page: https://viscom.uni-ulm.de/wsp

papers.title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
papers.abstract: Flow matching is a versatile framework for generative modeling that transports a source distribution to a target data distribution. A key advantage is its flexibility in the choice of source distribution, such as heavy-tailed and multimodal sources. Yet finite-step sampling guarantees for non-Gaussian sources remain limited. We establish a nonasymptotic convergence theory for Euler discretization of flow matching with linear interpolation. Suppose the source distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ has an everywhere positive, continuously differentiable density, finite total variance $\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}$, and an $L$-Lipschitz score. Using the population velocity field and a suitable time grid, this sampler achieves total variation error at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ iterations, provided the target distribution satisfies a mild second-moment condition. These assumptions cover, among many examples, source distributions such as multivariate Student's $t$ distributions with more than two degrees of freedom and finite Gaussian mixtures with shared covariance, while accommodating target distributions with neither a smooth density nor bounded support.

papers.title: Semi-global Convergence and Finite-Sample Error Bounds for Model Predictive Path Integral Control
papers.abstract: We investigate the global optimisation behaviour of Model Predictive Path Integral Control (MPPI) in the low-temperature setting. For objective functions with a unique global minimum and under weak additional assumptions, allowing non-convexity and non-smoothness, we establish semi-global convergence of the mean-field or population level MPPI iteration to this global optimum. We also establish finite-sample results that show that with high probability the MPPI iteration comes close to the global optimum and provide sample complexity results. Under slightly stronger assumptions, we make these results more quantitative and provide concrete bounds on the inverse temperature and number of samples. Finally, we illustrate the results on the classic LQR problem.

papers.title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

papers.title: Interpretation follows computation for deformed atomic nuclei
papers.abstract: The interpretation of nuclear levels in experiments and ab initio computations is challenging because it requires the production and analysis of many expectation values and transition strengths. Here we introduce an approach that yields directly interpretable states. Our ab initio coupled-cluster computations start from a reference state with axial symmetry and positive parity. Equation-of-motion techniques then yield intrinsic states with definite parity and angular-momentum projection onto the symmetry axis. Finally, the projection onto good angular momenta yields rotational bands based on these intrinsic states. In the neutron-rich nucleus $^{34}$Mg, where only the ground-state band is known, we find several low-lying positive- and negative-parity bands. The lowest, a $K^π=3^-$ band, is dominated by a single neutron particle-hole excitation rather than by octupole collectivity. These results challenge the common wisdom about how deformation and pairing work in nuclei.

papers.title: First Neumann eigenfunctions on piecewise smooth Jordan domains with convex corners
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonzero eigenfunction of the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded planar Jordan domain whose boundary consists of finitely many smooth arcs meeting at interior angles strictly between $0$ and $π$ has nonvanishing gradient in the interior; hence its extrema are attained only on the boundary. The eigenvalue may be multiple and the domain need not be convex; every convex polygon is included. The method adapts a recent Green-kernel approach for smooth domains.

papers.title: Aggregating soft-photon recoil with a positive finite-step sampler
papers.abstract: We model stochastic radiation reaction by aggregating soft photons into one positive recoil, retaining the local no-emission probability and two loss moments of the crossed-field QED kernel. Unlike Gaussian diffusion, the sampler preserves one-sided energy loss. Analytical synchrotron moments expose a finite-step cooling bias, which state feedback reduces. Laser and ion-channel tests probe excessive-loss risk and directed radiation spectra, providing a practical route to stochastic particle simulations without resolving individual soft emissions.

papers.title: Harish-Chandra isomorphism over arbitrary base rings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}$, and let $R$ be any commutative ring. We prove that Harish-Chandra projection induces a natural, strict filtered isomorphism $U_R(\mathfrak{g}_R)^{G_R} \simeq \operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathfrak{h}_R)^{W,\bullet}$, whereas the corresponding Chevalley restriction need not be surjective even over a field.

papers.title: On the semantics of conditional branching
papers.abstract: Motivated by the non-standard interpretations of if-then-else in probabilistic and quantum programs we review the different semantics of conditional branching and propose a unifying categorical structure for the interpretation of if-then-else. We show that many semantically important categories possess this structure, covering inter alia classical, probabilistic, quantum or non-deterministic computations. We examine algebraic structures related to and generated by this categorical structure, in particular on collections of predicates. In this setting we show that the skew-associativity rules of GKATs and barycentric algebras are two instances of a common skew-associativity rule.

papers.title: Curvature Integrability in Twinor Theory: An Ambitwistor Approach to the Twinor Googly Problem
papers.abstract: The twinor analogue of the googly problem is addressed through an ambitwistor structure defined by null autoparallels, retaining both chiralities, sources and torsion without requiring chiral null surfaces. Under the stated quotient, evaluation and descent assumptions, holomorphic affine sections reconstruct the twinor field equation $DY=J$. Correspondence-space cohomology realizes the contracted chiral and ladder equations, including the ladder's soldering coupling and mass-normalization source. For a prescribed non-normal conformal connection, infinity-twistor parallelism recovers the energy--momentum equation, supplemented by independent spin-current equations. These constructions give a conditional auxiliary formulation; constitutive sources and gravitational prescriptions remain dynamical input.

papers.title: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate Resilience: an Agentic AI Ecosystem
papers.abstract: EU-funded projects produce extensive evidence in the form of deliverables, reports, and case studies. However, this knowledge is typically scattered across projects and document structures, making it difficult to locate relevant, contextual information when making decisions. This paper introduces an Agentic AI Ecosystem that consolidates heterogeneous project documentation into a domain-aware knowledge base and provides adaptive access through an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline. Documents from three EU-funded projects (IMPETUS, NATALIE, and InnWater) are reconstructed into hierarchical section trees and indexed with structured metadata. Retrieval is supported by two domain-specific embedding models fine-tuned on domain data (water and climate). On top of this knowledge base, a ReAct-style controller iteratively orchestrates retrieval actions by allocating retrieval budget across domain collections and accumulating evidence until a stopping criterion is met. In a retrieval benchmark over the corpus, the proposed approach improves Mean Reciprocal Rank by 26.7% (relative) compared to a single-domain embedding baseline, indicating more consistent retrieval of relevant evidence to support cross-project knowledge synthesis and climate-resilient decision-making.

papers.title: Hook histories and a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual canonical Grothendieck functions
papers.abstract: We establish a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for power-sum multiplication in the dual canonical stable Grothendieck basis. The coefficients admit a closed boundary product formula and a signed combinatorial description by hook histories. We determine their exact support and prove an exact divisibility law for off-diagonal coefficients governed by the edge-connected components of the indexing skew diagram. We also obtain a hook expansion of power sums, an explicit binomial reduction to the dual stable rule, and a Grassmannian $K$-homological interpretation of the one-parameter specialization. Finally, we deduce complementary rules for power-sum multiplication in the canonical basis and the corresponding lowering operation in the dual canonical basis.

papers.title: Rethinking Utility in Differentially Private Visualization: A Channel-Centric Perspective
papers.abstract: Differential privacy (DP) is increasingly adopted to protect sensitive data in visualization, but understanding how privacy-induced noise affects visual representations remains fragmented. Prior work has examined the impact of DP noise on specific chart types, yet these findings are typically tied to particular chart types and evaluation settings, making it difficult to generalize across contexts. In parallel, visualization research has long established that visual channels, the visual properties of marks that encode data attributes, differ in perceptual effectiveness under noise-free conditions. However, these principles have not been systematically revisited under DP, where noise is deliberately introduced into the data to protect privacy. In this paper, we present a channel-centric perspective to reframe prior empirical and theoretical results. Our synthesis drawson prior findings to motivate a channel-read-mechanism hypothesis: the utility of DP visualizations may depend on the task-relevant reads made salient by visual channel configurations and DP mechanism choice jointly. Moreover, this perspective highlights the role of channel choice throughout the privacy-preserving visualization pipeline, from disclosure framing and DP algorithm design to utility evaluation and interpretation of noisy outputs. The synthesis also identifies gaps in the existing evaluation literature and highlights research opportunities for channel-aware DP visualization.

papers.title: Non-Binary Detector Error Models
papers.abstract: A key challenge in fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) is that the syndrome extraction circuits are themselves faulty. Such circuit-level noise is commonly described by a detector error model (DEM). In Stim and in almost all related works, DEMs are binary: every non-binary circuit error (e.g., CNOT gate), is decomposed into independent binary error mechanisms. In this work, we introduce non-binary DEMs, in which each fault location of the syndrome extraction circuit is modeled by one random variable over its original alphabet, e.g., the 16 two-qubit Pauli errors after a CNOT gate. We also propose a split-merge-regroup transformation that builds a compact non-binary DEM from any Clifford circuit by merging the error components that flip the same detectors and observables. Non-binary DEMs represent any Pauli channel exactly, whereas binary DEMs are exact only for channels that factorize into independent binary parts. When the channels factorize, we prove that binary and non-binary DEMs are equivalent under degenerate quantum maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) decoding, but not under quantum MAP decoding. Although the variables are non-binary, belief propagation (BP) still exchanges a single scalar message per edge. Our numerical results with surface, color and bivariate bicycle codes show that non-binary DEMs have two main advantages. First, their Tanner graphs have four to five times fewer edges, which is advantageous for hardware implementations. Second, their performance under BP, with and without OSD post-processing, is better than that of their binary counterparts, and BP with OSD runs up to $9.4\times$ faster in a CPU.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Statistical Mechanics: Physical Concepts & Mathematical Tools
papers.abstract: As anything not in equilibrium is, by definition, nonequilibrium, there is no universally agreed-upon set of topics that can constitute an exhaustive presentation of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics. At the same time, nonequilibrium statistical mechanics has transcended traditional physics to become a powerful language for complex systems. Prompted by an enthusiastic curiosity about complex systems, these cursory lecture notes attempt to elucidate some introductory concepts and techniques used in classical nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, which find successful applications not only in foundational physics, but also across other fields such as biology, ecology, economics, and sociology. Except for the specific synthesis and presentation of the material, which assumes basic familiarity with equilibrium statistical mechanics, the author claims no originality.

papers.title: Sensor-Free Shockable Rhythm Classification During CPR Using the Existing ECG Channel of Public-Access Automated External Defibrillators
papers.abstract: Automated external defibrillators (AEDs) are public-access devices intended for use by lay rescuers, yet they must pause chest compressions to analyze the rhythm because compressions corrupt the electrocardiogram (ECG). Removing this pause requires a method that uses the hardware already present in the device, fits within its processor budget, and meets the rhythm-recognition performance required for defibrillator approval. Existing approaches rely either on an auxiliary sensor, which entails a hardware redesign, or on an additional network that reconstructs the ECG before classification. This work classifies the compression-contaminated ECG directly, using only the existing ECG channel of the AED. A cascade of three compact convolutional networks trained with different class ratios verifies each decision with a second network biased toward the proposed outcome; disagreement yields an indeterminate outcome. Evaluated on an independent manufacturer-provided cohort of 464 subjects over 15 train-validation partitions, the cascade satisfies both adjudicable American Heart Association criteria under all six noise conditions at an eight-second window and a signal-to-artifact ratio of 0 dB, with sinus-rhythm specificity of 99.20-99.43% and other non-shockable specificity of 95.48-96.20%, leaving only 1.07-1.48% of segments indeterminate. The criteria are not met at -3 dB. Single networks matched in parameter count and inference cost do not reproduce this performance. Each decision evaluates two of the three networks and requires 6.68 ms on a single thread of a general-purpose processor, and eight-bit quantization reduces the model to 1.45 MiB without changing any compliance verdict. Thus, rhythm analysis during ongoing CPR can be implemented with the ECG hardware already present in public-access AEDs, without auxiliary sensing hardware, subject to validation on the target device.

papers.title: Constraint on anomalous $W^-W^+γ$ coupling in $\ell^\pm γ\slashed{E}$ final state at NLO QCD
papers.abstract: We study the anomalous $W^-W^+γ$ triple gauge couplings in the $pp\to \ell^\pmγ\slashed{E}$ channel at $\sqrt{s}=13$~TeV with next-to-leading order QCD corrections. Eight polarization asymmetries of the reconstructed $W$ boson, measured in four disjoint regions of $Δη_{\ellγ}$ and combined with the $m_{Wγ} \ge 1$ TeV distribution, are used to constrain the two CP-even and two CP-odd couplings. The bounds improve only marginally with increasing luminosity, far below the statistical expectation, while they degrade substantially when the systematic uncertainties are relaxed, showing that the sensitivity is systematically limited. A simultaneous four-parameter MCMC fit is performed to obtain marginalized limits. Relative to the CMS $WW+WZ$ combination, our bounds are significantly tighter for the CP-odd coupling $\widetildeλ_γ$ and competitive for $λ_γ$. The CP-odd results are also compared with the electron EDM limit, which constrains both couplings by roughly $2.5$ orders of magnitude beyond the collider reach.

papers.title: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
papers.abstract: Multimode optical fibres can image through a thin, flexible probe once their transmission matrix (TM) has been measured, but a TM is large and must be re-measured whenever the fibre moves. A compact model of feasible TMs would make storing and re-estimating them cheaper, so we ask how compactly TMs can be represented, and from how few measured TMs. Here we benchmark a permutation-equivariant autoencoder, pretrained on simulated fibres and adapted to measured TMs, against principal component analysis (PCA). At 62x compression, adapting the pretrained autoencoder with just two measured TMs reconstructs the TM of a 50um fibre well enough to focus light at 98% of the ideal enhancement, and it stays accurate when the TMs are shifted by 25 pixels or zoomed by 10%, which quickly degrades a linear basis. It is not, however, a better compressor: PCA is about ten times more accurate when fitted on all 163 real TMs (1.1% against 11.9% error on held-out TMs) and is already more accurate from ten. The autoencoder's value is as a prior when few or no real TMs exist: with none it reaches 29% error, against 91% for PCA fitted on the same simulation. Transfer to a different fibre is only partial. The most important extension, not yet tested, is to recover pixel-basis TMs from fewer measurements than a full TM, which would turn the pretrained prior from a compressor into a measurement-saving tool.

papers.title: SpecFlow: Flow Matching in the Acceleration Spectrum for Multi-Agent Trajectory Forecasting
papers.abstract: Multimodal trajectory forecasting must cover diverse future behaviors without sacrificing dynamical coherence. Most generative forecasters evolve frame-wise positions directly, leaving the relationships among position, velocity, and acceleration implicit. We present SpecFlow, a conditional flow-matching framework that treats the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) coefficients of future accelerations as its generative state. SpecFlow learns a transport from Gaussian noise to acceleration spectra and reconstructs velocity and position through fixed analytical integration initialized by the last observed state. A joint phase-space objective supervises all three kinematic levels. To represent destination uncertainty without future information, an endpoint predictor produces candidate destinations and confidence scores solely from observed context, and the highest-confidence candidate conditions the spectral denoiser. Alternating attention over trajectory hypotheses and agents captures multimodality and interaction. Under best-of-20 evaluation, SpecFlow achieves average minADE/minFDE of 0.15/0.22 on ETH/UCY, 0.69/0.86 at four seconds on NBA, and 7.38/11.57 on SDD. It establishes state-of-the-art results across all five ETH/UCY scenes and achieves the lowest four-second ADE on NBA with a tied-best FDE, while remaining competitive on SDD. Together, these results demonstrate that acceleration-spectrum flow matching provides an effective structured generative state across smooth pedestrian motion, coordinated multi-agent sports dynamics, and heterogeneous outdoor trajectories. Code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
papers.abstract: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide.

papers.title: GateTrace: Where Do Crowd Crossings Go Missing Under Occlusion?
papers.abstract: At large events, pedestrian tracking supports entrance and passageway counts, but totals hide which crossings were missed. In a stadium study, the system recorded about four in five clearly visible crossings but fewer than one in three mostly obscured crossings. The videos lacked trajectories annotated across frames, so we turned to MOT20, which provides pedestrian trajectories and visibility. We introduce GateTrace to locate missed crossings and assess changes to counting rules. It derives reference crossings from annotations under fixed rules, matches reports by person, direction, time and position, and traces misses through saved boxes and counting decisions. With a shared detector, ByteTrack, OC-SORT and BoT-SORT recover 38.9-46.7% of low-visibility reference crossings on development sequences, versus 98.1-99.0% at high visibility. The gap recurs on two further sequences under a protocol fixed in advance. Published outputs of MOT20-tuned BASE recover 63-78% at low visibility across both sequence groups. Losses stop at different stages across systems. Across four systems and both groups, 47-79% of low-visibility misses have no nearby output linked to the person or no possible crossing in the saved tracks. Removing later checks from BASE on development sequences leaves most misses unresolved and lowers precision against the fixed reference list from about 96% to 77%. Misses also remain among sampled reference crossings that two human annotators supported after checking the videos. GateTrace shows where crossings are lost and measures the recovery and precision costs of changing later checks. We will release the code and per-crossing records.

papers.title: A photon-number-conserving multimode framework for pulse propagation dynamics across zero nonlinearity: Kerr-Raman cooperation and competition
papers.abstract: Raman scattering in multimode fibers shifts pulse spectra to lower frequencies and transfers photons between spatial modes. When the nonlinear coefficient changes sign within the pulse spectrum, the ordinary generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) can give unphysical predictions. Existing photon-number-conserving formulations either treat a single mode or exclude Raman scattering. We develop a time-domain multimode GNLSE that conserves photon number, includes the full Raman response and remains well defined at the zero-nonlinearity frequency. For narrowband pulses with a constant positive nonlinear coefficient, the framework reduces to the standard multimode GNLSE with instantaneous Kerr and delayed Raman terms. We then apply the framework to three coherently excited modes whose spectra shift across the zero-nonlinearity frequency. The Kerr and Raman processes first cooperate and then compete. In the first stage, both processes transfer photons into the fundamental mode, contributing about 2\% and 43\% of the initial total photon number. In the second stage, Kerr transfer drives photons out of the fundamental mode, while Raman transfer drives photons back, contributing about $-27\%$ and $+15\%$, respectively. Consequently, the fundamental-mode photon fraction rises from 20\% to 65\% and then falls to 53\%. Kerr terms that leave the modal photon populations unchanged still reshape the fields and thereby enhance Raman transfer. Moreover, changing only the relative input phases can reverse the initial Raman-driven flow into the fundamental mode, even for identical modal spectra. Taken together, the results show how instantaneous and delayed nonlinear responses, together with intermodal phase, govern photon redistribution across zero nonlinearity.

papers.title: SEEC: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Self-Supervised External-Eye Representation Learning
papers.abstract: External-eye photography captures clinically relevant periocular anatomy at low acquisition cost, yet no large-scale standardized resource exists for evaluating self-supervised external-eye representations. We introduce a 4.35-million-image Standardized External-Eye Corpus (SEEC) derived from fourteen heterogeneous public face datasets, together with a benchmark for external-eye representation learning. For evaluation, we provide held-out evaluation distributions, landmark-annotated anatomical probe sets, and clinical disease-classification experiments spanning ptosis, thyroid eye disease, and craniofacial syndromes. We evaluate representations at two complementary levels: (a) the representation level, by assessing embedding geometry across multiple data distributions, and (b) the functional level, by assessing anatomical recovery, out-of-distribution anatomical transfer, and disease classification. Our models include ResNet-101 and ViT-B encoders pretrained using InfoNCE, VICReg, and LeJEPA objectives and compared with DINOv2 and MAE. Our results indicate that representation-level and functional-level evaluations are dissociable: broader embedding-space utilization does not consistently correspond to anatomical transfer or disease-classification performance, and no single encoder is universally optimal. Domain-specific external-eye encoders outperform DINOv2 and MAE on cross-dataset anatomical transfer despite being pretrained at substantially smaller scale, while external-eye-pretrained ViT models match or outperform these general-purpose baselines on frozen disease-classification probes. We release benchmark code, evaluation scripts, and preprocessing pipelines to reproduce SEEC at https://monkeygobah.github.io/seec-project/

papers.title: Beyond the Sink Interpretation: Radial Attention in Flow-Based VLA Policies
papers.abstract: Prior work calls the high attention on the first and last action tokens of a flow-based VLA policy a radial action sink, and uses these tokens to set the execution horizon. In language models, a sink is a token with high incoming attention, a small value, and little effect on the output. We test whether that profile holds, not the horizon rule, in one $π_{0.5}$ checkpoint on five RoboCasa tasks. The two endpoints receive 5.4% of action-key mass, 1.4 percentage points above their uniform share, and rotary positional encoding produces this excess: directly in shallow layers and through upstream action-token RoPE deeper in the network. The endpoints do not fit the sink profile. Their value norms stay near the action-token mean in all 18 layers. On 250 paired episodes, masking them or zeroing their values changes success by less than 4 points, and replacing their value directions with those of another observation lowers it by 3.2 to 7.2 points across three donors, whereas the same replacement on two non-endpoint tokens in the executed prefix lowers it by 28.4 points. The token that does fit the sink profile on mass and value norm is the prefix BOS; on this checkpoint, zeroing its value raises success in two paired runs, by +13.2 points (95% CI [+7.0, +19.4]) and +6.0 points ([+0.2, +11.8]). Inside the action chunk, a relative-offset routing profile estimated on other tasks keeps 75% of action-token spread and keeps closed-loop success on three held-out tasks (42.7% against a 38.7% baseline), while uniform or shuffled routing drops success to 3-4%. High attention mass alone does not tell what a token does.

papers.title: A Complete Geometric Message-Passing Architecture for Point Clouds
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional point clouds are a fundamental data modality, and a large family of machine learning architectures has been developed to respect their natural symmetries to rigid motions and permutations. A principled way to compare these architectures, which vary widely in complexity and cost, is through their expressive power. That is, an architecture is complete if it can distinguish any two inputs not related by the symmetries it respects. Simple distance-based message-passing networks are known to be incomplete, and while there exist complete alternatives, they typically rely on computationally intensive mechanisms like high-order representations of the rotation group or higher-order Weisfeiler-Leman-type tests. In this work, we devise a novel, simple, equivariant message-passing architecture for point clouds, and prove that it is complete. We complement our theoretical result with experiments showing that our architecture separates challenging point clouds that distance-based message passing provably cannot distinguish. Our results suggest that high-order equivariant features may not be necessary to enhance the expressivity of point cloud architectures, and can help settle completeness for other equivariant architectures for which such results are currently unknown. We give initial evidence for this by proving completeness of a slightly modified version of SEGNN.

papers.title: Evidence from a Multi-Regime Causal Discovery Benchmark: UCMT Algorithms, Comparative Performance, and Controlled Ablation Studies
papers.abstract: We present an internal, pre-registered evaluation of the UCMT causal discovery algorithm family alongside established alternatives across heterogeneous benchmark regimes, complemented by a separately pre-registered, controlled study of UCMT v2 Global components. The contribution is both empirical and methodological: a family-stratified comparison of three actively developed algorithm configurations and targeted evidence about which internal stages affect their outcomes. In the main benchmark, UCMT v2 Global has higher directed F1 than NOTEARS and DAGMA in selected real, semi-synthetic and Gaussian-network comparisons at the paired-run level, while trailing leading permutation-search methods in other settings. The BOSS-based UCMT v4 produces a CSuite-specific directed-F1 improvement over BOSS (mean paired difference +0.279; pair-level Holm p < 0.001), but the dataset-level adjusted result is not significant (p = 0.188). In a separate fixed-skeleton ablation, UCMT v2 Global exceeds an adapted R^2-SortnRegress orientation baseline on standardized iSCM data (directed F1 0.537 vs 0.468, dataset-level Holm p = 0.031); absolute orientation accuracy is 0.563 and there is no established broad advantage over RESIT, ANM or DirectLiNGAM. Controlled ablations show that sparsity and BIC-based refinement materially affect some outcomes, whereas the examined arbitration and automatic regime-selection mechanisms do not yield confirmed general improvements. We report performance shortcomings, multiple-testing correction, runtime costs, evaluation limitations and reproducibility checks. The results support UCMT as an implemented and empirically investigated algorithm family, not a claim of overall superiority, independent validation or demonstrated commercial impact.

papers.title: Efficient Classical Algorithms for Ground Energy Estimation of Fermions with Conjugate-Pair Orbital Interactions
papers.abstract: Estimating the ground energy of interacting fermions is central to quantum many-body physics, and recent quantum algorithms provide polynomial-time guarantees for some structured families. Classical approaches commonly rely on quantum Monte Carlo, where the sign problem is a major obstacle. However, even when a nonnegative expansion without sign problem is available, rigorous guarantees for rapid mixing are still far from well understood. In this paper, we give an efficient classical randomized algorithm for approximating the ground energy of fermionic Hamiltonians with conjugate hopping matrices and conjugate-paired orbital interactions, which includes the attractive Hubbard models. This guarantee not only holds without a physical spectral gap or a weak-coupling assumption, but also covers interactions beyond onsite density attractions. Technically, we first reduce ground-energy estimation to partition-function estimation and then use a discretization with controlled energy error to obtain a nonnegative weighted sum of squared determinant moduli and then apply the Chen--Liu log-concave counting theorem. In addition, we obtain a sharper arithmetic bound by controlling how many independent sampling runs and matrix updates are needed, and using sparse matrices to reduce the cost of each update.

papers.title: Imaginary-Time Density Correlations Encode Quantum Entropy and Free Energy
papers.abstract: In the classical limit, maximum-entropy inference yields an estimate of the excess entropy from the static structure factor through a single momentum sum. Quantum mechanically this estimate fails, because interactions also change the kinetic energy, while delocalization and exchange add information that equal-time correlations do not contain. We show that imaginary-time density correlations contain this information, and that with them the classical relation carries over to quantum systems. Such correlations are available from path-integral simulations and X-ray Thomson scattering. Relative-entropy inference over imaginary-time paths, with an ideal Bose or Fermi gas as reference, gives closed forms for the excess entropy and free energies, within the same Gaussian approximation as the classical relation. They recover the classical result and estimate entropy that the classical relation misses. We test them on weakly interacting bosons, interacting fermions on a ring, and the warm dense electron gas. The closed forms need only imaginary-time density correlations and their ideal-gas reference at a single state point, without using the interaction potential. Our approach can extend other classical entropy estimators to quantum systems.

papers.title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
papers.abstract: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer's overall activity with timed steps whose narration adapts to varying perceptual demands and marks key moments at specific timestamps. We develop a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline that establishes event structure before expanding step descriptions, yielding 50,000 training examples from eight egocentric video sources. Complementary rewards assess factual accuracy and coverage, measure step-level temporal alignment, and penalize fragmented or redundant narration, guiding caption refinement through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To improve the reliability of factual supervision, we supplement caption references with pose-derived motion facts when sensor data are available. Across five egocentric benchmarks, EgoCaptioner achieves leading performance among evaluated open-source models in caption quality, caption-conditioned question answering, and temporal alignment. It also surpasses Gemini 3.1 Pro on PhysCapBench and all evaluated proprietary baselines on Minerva-Ego under the caption-to-QA protocol. Ablations support the complementary roles of factual and temporal rewards and show that coarse-to-fine annotation provides more effective supervision than single-pass annotation.

papers.title: Twinor Theory in the Newton--Hooke Limit: A Nonrelativistic Schrödinger Equation for Arbitrary Spin
papers.abstract: The Newton--Hooke limit of the massive twinor field equations is derived at fixed particle mass and fixed cosmological acceleration per unit displacement. On a static torsion-free background, removal of the rest energy separates the leading spin amplitude from a finite sequence of auxiliary spinors. For every positive integer rank $2s$, a regular limit of exact solutions satisfies a first-order hierarchy. Its lowest two equations give a necessary Schrödinger equation for the leading amplitude, with a curvature term from the ordered spatial derivatives and a source determined by two projections of the relativistic source. The higher equations impose additional conditions. On the homogeneous Newton--Hooke background with trivial internal connection and nonzero cosmological acceleration parameter, vanishing of all limiting contracted sources forces the leading amplitude to vanish for $s\geq\tfrac32$. A separate reduction of the scalar wave equation gives the spin-zero case.

papers.title: Optimal Preemption: Guaranteeing Information Freshness in Mean Age and Beyond
papers.abstract: Once a status update enters service, age-optimal policies must wait for it, even when heavy-tailed delays inflate the Age of Information (AoI). We develop a framework in which the sender may preempt the update in service and sample a fresh one, under general service-time distributions and explicit action costs. Our framework covers sources that generate updates at will as well as random update arrivals. Under nondecreasing age costs, we prove that, with preemption, a finite mean delay suffices for a finite average age even under infinite delay variance. We show the optimality of constant service-age thresholds from prior work for exponential service, and exhibit numerically that for general delays the optimal preemption rule depends on both the AoI and the elapsed service time. Under an action-cost budget, we further minimize the Value at Risk (VaR), which bounds the AoI except for a prescribed fraction of time, and the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR), the mean AoI over that fraction. We reduce both to the same optimality equations without enlarging the state space. Under Pareto and log-normal delays, our algorithm TAILOR keeps the average cost bounded as delay variance grows, while optimal non-preemptive sampling diverges. With optimal preemption, a more variable network can allow fresher data than a steadier one of equal mean delay.

papers.title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
papers.abstract: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 $μ$W and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth. These results establish a promising route toward high-power, phase-coherent short-wavelength frequency combs for precision spectroscopy, including searches for the nuclear transition in trapped $^{229}$Th ions.

papers.title: Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate broad generalization across tasks and domains. However, comparable generalization in robot manipulation remains challenging. Heterogeneity in robot embodiments, task formulations, geometric conventions, and action interfaces fragments interaction experience across benchmarks and hardware. We rethink robot skill learning through alignment: Can heterogeneous interactions across benchmarks and embodiments jointly improve one shared skillset for robot manipulation? We propose UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings. Specifically, UniCraft represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots. It organizes tasks from different benchmarks in a canonical format, allowing interaction feedback to jointly refine shared skills and the orchestration policy that guides their selection and composition, without any demonstrations or model weight updates. We interleave tasks from 3 benchmarks and 6 embodiments, collecting 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model. During training, UniCraft improves pooled task success on unseen scenarios and tasks by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO, 10.8-13.3 on RoboTwin 2.0, and 3.1-14.4 on RoboCasa365 (Epochs 1-3). After training, with the learned skills frozen, UniCraft demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 4 new robot embodiments and 5 additional agent models on robosuite and RoboDojo.

papers.title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
papers.abstract: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions. In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.

papers.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
papers.abstract: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar interactions exists at all orders, represented by a finite number of effective even forms. 3. The higher-derivative contact-term sector can be constructed from a finite set of basic tensor structures using polynomials in derivative symbols. We introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity considerations.

papers.title: Effect of coupling asymmetry on the spontaneous decay and entanglement of two atoms in a common cavity
papers.abstract: We investigate the dynamics and the spontaneous decay of two identical two-level atoms into the vacuum in a cavity at low temperature. We analytically derive the survival probability and the amplitudes of the state of the system by calculating the exact self-energy when the atoms are both initially excited. It is found that moderate asymmetry enhances the decay of the survival probability and increases the entanglement production in either lossless and lossy cavities.

papers.title: Lower-Mass Giants Can Spare Inner Planets during High-Eccentricity Migration
papers.abstract: The survival of an inner planet next to a close-in giant is commonly used to argue against high-eccentricity migration (HEM), because the eccentric giant is expected to destabilize the inner system. Existing survival calculations have concentrated on Jupiter-mass migrants, although several Jupiter-sized close-in giants with nearby companions have sub-Jovian masses. We use dissipative three-body integrations to measure the collision-survival boundary at seven giant masses from $0.25$ to $1.0,M_{\rm Jup}$ and combine it with uncompressed equilibrium-tide circularization times. At fixed physical periapse, lower giant mass weakens the forcing of the inner orbit and shifts the survival boundary inward. It also shortens the circularization time for a common radius and tidal prescription. These dynamical and tidal limits enclose a viable HEM region in which a sub-Jovian giant can circularize within a system age while retaining an ultra-short-period companion. We screen known companion-hosting close-in giants and perform system-specific integrations of WASP-132; every current candidate lies outside the region. A future system inside it would show directly that HEM can produce a close-in giant while preserving an inner planet, converting companion survival into positive evidence for this formation channel.

papers.title: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Page-Wootters construction in which time is a quantum clock reading and the global system state is stationary, we propose a quantum circuit that explores the observable consequences of treating measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. We place two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in a coherent superposition using a schedule qubit. We show that, for a fixed drive strength, the interference visibility between the two schedules depends only on the time offset between them, not on the number of intermediate measurements taken. Then we show that, for one schedule-readout outcome, the Zeno trend reverses, predicting a result that complements the standard Zeno probability. We propose a circuit implementation with physical memory qubits and show that measuring the memory register's joint $X$-basis parity distinguishes a coherent schedule from a classical or dephased one. We give the gate count and an error budget for a superconducting-qubit implementation. The Page-Wootters picture motivates this protocol and provides an equivalent stationary representation, although the predictions follow from the standard circuit description without requiring a relational-time interpretation. This is consistent with the Page-Wootters framework recovering standard quantum dynamics through correlations between a clock and the rest of the system.

papers.title: Fast Self-Supervised Generative CT Denoising via Few-Step Sampling
papers.abstract: Low-dose and thin-slice computed tomography (CT) images suffer from elevated noise that obscures anatomical detail, while clean references for supervised denoising are often unavailable. Although Noise2Noise permits self-supervised training from noisy pairs, direct regression tends to oversmooth fine structure. Averaging multiple independently generated samples mitigates this blur, though repeating multi-step diffusion sampling is costly. We introduce Noise2Noise with Improved Mean Flow (N2N-iMF) to accelerate this process via few-step sampling. N2N-iMF learns to generate one noisy image conditioned on its paired counterpart; at inference, independent outputs are sampled and averaged to suppress noise. We evaluated image quality and sampling efficiency on simulated thin-slice brain and low-dose abdominal CT across four sampling methods and averaging counts from 1 to 20, and validated the approach on real-world photon-counting CT (PCCT) brain scans. With ten samples per conditioning input and three network evaluations per sample, N2N-iMF achieved a mean absolute error of 2.60 HU on brain CT and 14.02 HU on abdominal CT, outperforming 50-evaluation denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM) sampling (2.91 and 14.53 HU). On the same GPU, per-output generation time dropped from 7.29 to 0.43 s. Across eight PCCT cases, N2N-iMF reached a mean gray-white matter contrast-to-noise ratio of 1.341, versus 0.916 for Noise2Noise and 1.176 for DDIM. N2N-iMF accelerates self-supervised generative CT denoising without distillation while keeping the number of averaged outputs adjustable at inference.

papers.title: From Benchmarks to the Bench: Preference, Correspondence and Selectivity in Bidirectional Drug-Target Screening
papers.abstract: Identifying active molecules for known targets and potential targets for existing drugs is central to drug discovery and repurposing. Drug-target interaction (DTI) models can rank vast numbers of drug-target pairs, but limited experimental capacity restricts testing to a small number of candidates. We compared the bidirectional recommendations of 13 released systems across 711 molecular structures of FDA-approved drugs and 614 human proteins. For the same target or drug, pairs of models produced completely disjoint Top-10 molecule and protein lists in 77.8% and 70.1% of comparisons, respectively. Even where recommendations overlapped, agreement between some systems largely reflected recurring preferences for the same candidates. Published inhibition measurements for 79 molecules and 65 kinases revealed that some systems enriched active candidates, yet their hit yields changed little when recommendations were matched to different drugs or targets, whereas other systems lost substantially more hits. Some of the former systems also rarely ranked both molecules and kinases correctly when two drugs favoured different kinases. We further retrained the same architecture on the same data, with the training objective fixed and random seeds varied. Despite similar test performance, mean pairwise Top-10 overlap on a separate screening catalogue was about two candidates. Our study moves DTI model evaluation beyond benchmark performance to assess whether model predictions can guide meaningful experimental decisions in drug discovery and target identification.

papers.title: Entanglement, records, and quantum recovery in qubit chains
papers.abstract: We investigate entanglement, readable records and quantum recovery using an exactly solvable chain of sequentially interacting qubits. For weak interactions, entanglement reaches a later environment site before that site carries an equally strong local record. The leading local record is encoded in an off-diagonal element of the reduced density matrix and can be detected by a Pauli measurement, while a population measurement gives a higher-order signal. We further characterize the accessibility of the relative phase through joint transverse correlations and derive the optimal fidelity for recovering an unknown quantum state from the system and an accessible environment fragment. We show that interactions acting only within the environment can redistribute readable records and change the region required for quantum recovery without affecting the reduced state of the system.

papers.title: Contactless Estimation of Respiratory Frequency Using 3D-CNN on Thermal Images
papers.abstract: Monitoring physiological parameters such as respiratory rate ($f_R$) is essential for diagnosing and managing various pathological conditions. Thermal imaging offers a promising contactless alternative to traditional methods, which often rely on partially invasive sensors or obtrusive wearable systems. However, existing approaches for $f_R$ estimation from thermal signals typically require extensive pre-processing and manual or semi-automatic region-of-interest (ROI) tracking, limiting their practical applicability. This study proposes a deep learning-based method for estimating $f_R$ directly from thermal videos, eliminating the need for complex pre-processing and ROI tracking. A 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) is developed to operate on raw thermal video data. To address challenges related to small datasets, the model is trained using data augmentation and transfer learning from synthetic datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a validation $R^2$ score of approximately 0.61 on both pre-processed and raw thermal videos. By simplifying the workflow, this method holds promise for enhancing the feasibility of thermal imaging in real-world applications, such as remote healthcare and driver monitoring in automotive applications.

papers.title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence
papers.abstract: World models are increasingly used to simulate physical interactions, but training a separate model for each environment limits scalability. Cross-environment prediction requires identifying the current physical rule, which appearance alone may not reveal. We therefore study visual calibration: using object motion and interactions in a short video as direct evidence to infer the current rule and predict motion under that rule from a different initial state. However, differences in data availability across physical conditions can yield a long-tailed training distribution, biasing models toward common rules even when evidence supports rare ones. To study this challenge, we introduce TailWorld, which evaluates the transfer of demonstrated rules across initial states while independently controlling training imbalance and calibration informativeness. The benchmark compares predictions with two reference futures from the same prediction initial state, one following the demonstrated rule and the other a common rule, to measure prediction bias toward common dynamics. We further propose Rule Inference for Transfer (RIFT), which learns how different rules affect object motion, infers the current rule from calibration interactions, and applies it to prediction from a new initial state. RIFT explicitly controls the influence of training frequency on rule inference, allowing sufficiently informative observational evidence to support rare rules. Experiments on TailWorld show that RIFT improves prediction accuracy and physical consistency across varying training imbalances and distribution shifts, with gains in predicting rare dynamics.

papers.title: Interpreting the Morbidity Gap
papers.abstract: The Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study now reports the morbidity gap (MG), life expectancy minus healthy life expectancy, as an indicator in its own right. Writing MG as the expected cumulative rate of years lived with disability (YLDs) at the life-table age at death, we use stochastic dominance results to show what MG measures, how it responds to mortality and how it relates to the YLDs of the current population. We show the following. (a) A YLD profile gives an MG no larger than another's under every life table if and only if its cumulative YLD rate is nowhere higher. (b) With YLD rates fixed, lower mortality at every age widens MG, so that removing a risk factor that raises mortality reduces MG by less than its contribution to MG in GBD's risk factor attribution. (c) A family of results gives easily interpretable conditions on the age structure of the population for the crude YLD rate to be above or below the life-table YLD rate, which is MG divided by life expectancy, and these conditions change with population ageing. We illustrate the results for Singapore, where MG widened from 8.9 to 11.2 years between 1990 and 2023.

papers.title: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders
