We also relate IS-captures to the cubic Principal Hyperbolic Domain and its closure (by definition, the \emph{cubic Principal Hyperbolic Domain} consists of cubic hyperbolic polynomials with Jordan curve Julia sets) and prove that, in the slice of cubic polynomials given by a fixed multiplier at one of the fixed points, the closure of the cubic principal hyperbolic domain might possibly only have bounded complementary domains $U$ such that (1) critical points of $f\in U$ are distinct and belong to $J(f)$, and (2) $J(f)$ has positive Lebesgue measure and carries an invariant line field.

papers.title: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that any area-preserving $C^r$-diffeomorphism of a two-dimensional surface displaying an elliptic fixed point can be $C^r$-perturbed to one exhibiting a chaotic island whose metric entropy is positive, for every $1\le r\le \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Herman stating that the identity map of the disk can be $C^\infty$-perturbed to a conservative diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy. This implies also that the Chirikov standard map for large and small parameter values can be $C^\infty$-approximated by a conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy (a weak version of Sinai's positive metric entropy conjecture). Finally, this sheds light onto a Herman's question on the density of $C^r$-conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy: we show the existence of a dense set formed by conservative diffeomorphism which either are weakly stable (so, conjecturally, uniformly hyperbolic) or display a chaotic island of positive metric entropy.

papers.title: Morita bundle gerbes
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to give a survey of the theory of bundle gerbes. We describe how local Morita equivalences replace a cocycle of matrix algebras and bimodules by a cocycle of complex lines. A positive-rank gerbe module identifies its module category with modules over an Azumaya bundle. We determine the Brauer classes represented by matrix degrees dividing powers of a prescribed integer, and compare Morita equivalence with unital UHF stabilization on the two-sphere. For Morita 2-bundle gerbes we carry out the reduction through the associator and the equivalences of cocycles. This identifies their equivalence classes on good-cover bases with fourth integral cohomology.

papers.title: Residue Automata Modulo $3^k$, Syracuse Random Variables, and Terminal-Branch Bias in Collatz Trajectories
papers.abstract: We study the residues modulo $3^k$ visited by trajectories of the accelerated Collatz map $T(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even), $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ ($n$ odd), starting from the six ``recurrent forms'' $9n+r$, $r\in\{1,2,4,5,7,8\}$. (i)~We give the exact transition automaton on these forms and its extension to every modulus $3^k$, and prove that for integers drawn from a complete residue system modulo $2^j3^k$ the first $j$ residues modulo $3^k$ form \emph{exactly} a Markov chain; its stationary law is Tao's Syracuse random variable, so the form $9n+8$ receives the fraction $22/63$ of all visits. (ii)~We determine the spectrum of this chain completely: its characteristic polynomial is $(x-1)\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\bigl(x^{2\cdot 3^i}-4^{-3^i}\bigr)$, so every non-trivial eigenvalue has modulus exactly $\tfrac12$ for every $k$. We prove that the mixing time lies between $k\log_2\frac32$ and $2k+O(\sqrt{k})$, show that the stationary mass of the class $-1 \bmod 3^k$ is at least $\tfrac43 2^{-k}$, and present numerical evidence for a cutoff at $k\log_2 3$. (iii)~We explain the strong bias observed in the residue class of the first power of~$2$ met by a trajectory: this class is determined by the last odd term $q_k=(4^k-1)/3$ through $k \bmod 3$; three of the six classes contain only powers of~$2$, a fourth has $O(\log^2N)$ elements up to $N$, and the remaining two are unions of predecessor sets of the $q_k$. Computations for $n\le 4\times10^{9}$ give the frequencies $0.9761$ and $0.0239$. (iv)~We formulate an \emph{octave law}---the expected number of orbit points in $[y,2y)$ lying in a class $r \bmod 3^k$ tends to $\frac{2\log 2}{\log(4/3)}$ times the Syracuse probability of $r$---and support it by exhaustive and Monte Carlo computation.

papers.title: Light propagation in dielectric materials: a microscopic derivation of the refractive index and of the extinction theorem
papers.abstract: We present a compact, self-contained derivation of the field established inside a dielectric by an incident light wave, starting from the picture of the material as a collection of polarizable atoms (or molecules) in vacuum, each driven by the incident field and by the fields re-radiated by all the others. Following the integral-equation route of Goldberger and Watson, the same few lines of calculation yield the Lorentz local field, the Lorentz-Lorenz relation between the refractive index and the atomic polarizability, and the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem: the incident wave is cancelled inside the medium by a field radiated by the induced dipoles and replaced by a wave travelling at $c/n$. The dilute limit is connected to the forward-scattering amplitude, the optical theorem and Rayleigh scattering. We then discuss, for a planar interface, in what sense reflection and refraction are a bulk effect for s-polarized light and a combination of bulk and surface (bound-charge) effects for p-polarized light, and why that surface term must not be confused with the local-field correction, although both stem from the same depolarization mathematics. Finally, a small coupled-dipole simulation of a random, finite collection of point dipoles checks the self-consistent local-field relation numerically. SI units are used throughout. The material is intended for an advanced undergraduate course on electromagnetism and optics.

papers.title: Fixed point theorems in plane continua with applications
papers.abstract: We present proofs of basic results, including those developed by Harold Bell, for the plane fixed point problem: does every map of a non-separating plane continuum have a fixed point? Some of these results had been announced much earlier by Bell but without accessible proofs. We define the concept of the variation of a map on a simple closed curve and relate it to the index of the map on that curve: Index = Variation + 1. A fixed point theorem for positively oriented, perfect maps of the plane is obtained. This generalizes results announced by Bell in 1982. A continuous map of an interval to the real line which sends the endpoints in opposite directions has a fixed point. We generalize this to maps on non-invariant continua in the plane under positively oriented maps of the plane (with appropriate boundary conditions). These methods imply that in some cases non-invariant continua in the plane are degenerate. This has important applications in complex dynamics. E.g., a special case of our results shows that if $X$ is a non-separating invariant subcontinuum of the Julia set of a polynomial $P$ containing no fixed Cremer points and exhibiting no local rotation at all fixed points, then $X$ must be a point. It follows that impressions of some external rays to polynomial Julia sets are degenerate.

papers.title: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
papers.abstract: Generating physically based rendering (PBR) texture maps for a 3D mesh from a single reference image is highly ambiguous, as the observed appearance entangles material identity, surface reflectance, and illumination. While current generative methods produce realistic albedo maps, they still struggle to infer accurate metallic and roughness attributes for relighting. We present UltraTex, a cascaded multi-view framework that moves beyond appearance matching by integrating physical knowledge into multi-view diffusion-based PBR generation. UltraTex first jointly predicts albedo and world-space shading normals to generate more detailed albedo maps, and then predicts metallic-roughness (MR) maps conditioned on the generated albedo, reference image, and material semantic priors. To inject material semantics, a lightweight adapter transforms hidden-layer features of a vision-language model (VLM) into intrinsic material representation tokens, providing part-level knowledge anchors for MR estimation. To model material-light interaction, photometric representation alignment guides intermediate diffusion features toward ground-truth material renderings under controlled lighting. This makes metallic and roughness variations observable through highlight intensity, specular sharpness, and local reflectance contrast, providing stronger guidance for fine-grained material prediction without explicit lighting supervision. Extensive experiments show that UltraTex generates high-quality textures and outperforms existing open-source and commercial methods in visual fidelity, material accuracy, and physical plausibility.

papers.title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human video and robot trajectories, $Z$-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.

papers.title: Map-Level Inference of Primordial Gravitational Waves from the CMB with Spherical Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We train a spherical graph convolutional network to infer the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ directly from multifrequency cosmic microwave background (CMB) $B$-mode maps on the cut sky. We test the network on simulations of a generic ground-based experiment including lensed CMB, inhomogeneous noise, and stochastic Galactic dust and synchrotron emission. We compare the network with a multifrequency bandpower likelihood built from the same 20,000 simulations used to train it. Working directly on the maps, with no power-spectrum estimation or component separation, the network reduces the root-mean-square error on $r$ by a factor of 1.3 and gives well-calibrated 68% intervals 1.2 times narrower than the likelihood with the same prior. Saliency maps show that the network learns to favor the deepest regions of the sky and the cleanest frequency channels without being given the survey depth. Both approaches are tied to the foreground model they are built on: the network generalizes to some alternative foreground models without retraining, but not to a three-dimensional dust model with line-of-sight variations. The network can be extended to marginalize over foreground models by training on a broad family, making direct map-level neural inference a promising route to $r$ for future $B$-mode analyses.

papers.title: LEMUR: A Searchable Web Archive of Deep Chandra Images of Galaxies and Galaxy Clusters
papers.abstract: We present LEMUR, a publicly accessible archive of uniformly reduced, deep Chandra images of 2,569 galaxies and galaxy clusters (including groups), comprising 5,505 ACIS observations and 138.8 Ms of exposure. By combining the publicly available imaging observations of each target, we provide background-subtracted, exposure-corrected images in broad, soft, and hard bands at the native ACIS pixel scale of 0.492 arcsec. Our primary goal is to make the wealth of archival Chandra observations accessible to researchers without requiring specialized expertise in X-ray data reduction. Each observation is reprocessed with CIAO, filtered for background flares, and reduced with settings chosen to preserve faint diffuse emission; the merged images are exposure corrected and background subtracted using the ACIS blank-sky backgrounds in a broad (0.5-7.0 keV), a soft (0.5-2.0 keV), and a hard (2.0-7.0 keV) band. For every object, we measure an X-ray center at the peak of its diffuse emission, and we provide a morphological similarity search based on embeddings from the AstroCLIP foundation model, in which nearest neighbors share cool-core status in 73% of matched cluster pairs, compared with 51% by chance. Photometry of 275 point sources agrees with the Chandra Source Catalog to within 3% in the broad band. The images, along with their counts images, background models, exposure maps, and quick-look stamps, are available through a searchable web archive at https://lemur-archive.lemur-xray.workers.dev/. The catalog tables are archived on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24351915), and all code is open source at https://github.com/crhea93/Lemur.

papers.title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
papers.abstract: Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an additional downstream classifier. We propose Jailbreak Detection with Prototype Inference (JDPI), which uses binary safety labels to construct harmful and benign prototypes and makes predictions from relative prototype distances. JDPI uses only binary safety labels for encoder adaptation, prototype construction, and validation. In our setup, it uses fewer labeled examples than the classifier baseline (Method A) by avoiding the separate split used to train the downstream classifier. Across four benchmarks covering different input formats, contrastive fine-tuning improves JDPI's detection accuracy by 9.1-18.0 percentage points. Using the same encoder, JDPI achieves slightly higher ROC-AUC on one benchmark and stays within 0.017 of the baseline across all four. With dataset-specific adaptation, JDPI exceeds the released Llama Guard 3-8B baseline by 0.173-0.310 in ROC-AUC across the four benchmarks. In multi-turn replay on TomGibbs, JDPI uses accumulated user history as the conversation unfolds, achieving higher conversation-level accuracy than when it uses the current turn alone. Across 12 directed transfers, JDPI outperforms the classifier by an average of 1.59 percentage points in accuracy, demonstrating stronger cross-dataset robustness.

papers.title: Exact Parent Hamiltonians for Partially Magnetized Chiral Spin Liquids
papers.abstract: Chiral spin liquids (CSLs) are paradigmatic fractionalized phases, yet simple exact parent Hamiltonians for them remain scarce. In this work, we construct exact spin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs realizing various bosonic topological orders. Our construction relies on an exact Hubbard-type parent Hamiltonian for bosonic lattice fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, valid at arbitrary repulsive interaction strengths. Taking the on-site repulsion to infinity and applying local boson-spin mappings yields exact parent Hamiltonians for the CSLs. Our two-spin construction generalizes the Kalmeyer-Laughlin spin Hamiltonian to a broader class of bosonic FQH model states, including Abelian states and non-Abelian parton states. We derive controlled microscopic realizations of these two-spin Hamiltonians via second-order superexchange in generalized spinful Hofstadter-Hubbard models with tailored hoppings and interactions. With more general local constraints and interactions, boson-spin mappings yield exact higher-spin and multispin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs.

papers.title: Low Moments, Small Balls and Star Discrepancy
papers.abstract: Let $D_P$ be the discrepancy function of a configuration $P$ of $N$ points in the $d$-dimensional unit cube, and let $\|D_P\|_q$ be its $L^q$ discrepancy. We prove that for all fixed $d\ge2$ and $0<q\le1$ the $L^q$ discrepancy of every configuration of $N\ge2$ points is at least $c_{d,q}(\log N)^{(d-1)/2}$ with a constant $c_{d,q}>0$. This bound is sharp; together with the classical results for $q>1$, it determines the minimal order of the $L^q$ discrepancy for every $0<q<\infty$ in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for $q=1$ it answers Chen's problem on the sharp lower bound for the $L^1$ discrepancy in dimension $d\ge3$. We prove the small ball inequality for Haar functions in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$ and for arbitrary real coefficients with the conjectured power of $n$, up to a polylogarithmic factor; here $2^{-n}$ is the smallest volume of the dyadic boxes involved. The method also extends to a class of piecewise polynomial mother functions. For the $L^\infty$ discrepancy $\|D_P\|_\infty=ND^*(P)$, where $D^*(P)$ is the star discrepancy, we prove the conjectured lower bound $c(\log N)^{3/2}$ in dimension three, and the lower bound $(\log N)^{d/2}$ up to a power of $\log\log N$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge4$. Finally, we construct $N$-point sets whose $L^\infty$ discrepancy is $O_d((\log N)^{d-1-1/16})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$; this disproves the conjectured optimality of the order $(\log N)^{d-1}$ of the classical constructions.

papers.title: On the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture
papers.abstract: We extend our results on Zhao's conjectural basis to finite multiple zeta values modulo arbitrary prime powers and to the corresponding completed algebra. As a consequence, the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture, which gives a precise description of relations modulo arbitrary prime powers in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values, follows from the dimension and direct-sum conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values. We also prove Rosen's lifting conjecture under the dimension conjecture for finite multiple zeta values. The proofs use confluence relations and $p$-adic associators and do not use motivic theory.

papers.title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
papers.abstract: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise. The theory makes five claims: value is governed by calibration rather than by activity, speed, agreement, or tenure; calibration leaves observable traces in behavioral telemetry; those traces are non-diagnostic on their own, because the fast, low-revision signature of a calibrated expert is indistinguishable from that of a confident novice until it is gated by outcomes; human calibration and a model's self-knowledge are the same construct, so the joint system should defer to whichever agent is better calibrated on each item; and individual calibration is causally identifiable only above the level of the single judgment. We ground each claim in a six-month production window of an AI-assisted accounting system (541621 reviewer events, 483 reviewers), and find that a purely behavioral expertise profile inverts the ground truth, scoring an overconfident cohort (5.2 percent correction survival) higher than genuine experts (99.2 percent); that reviewer quality is flat across tenure, so the trait is not learned on the job; and that the same calibration logic that separates good from bad reviewers, applied to the model, concentrates 92.5 percent of human effort on genuine errors. We close with the boundary the theory must respect: under majority-vote aggregation, individual causal value is unidentifiable.

papers.title: Sharp Complexity Thresholds for Network Cournot Competition
papers.abstract: We determine the approximation complexity of network Cournot equilibrium as a function of demand degree and the number of firms sharing a market. For common, nonincreasing concave polynomial inverse demands, convex quadratic costs of firms' allocation vectors, and rational total capacities, high-precision approximation is polynomial-time solvable for cubic demands, regardless of market size. Quartic demands remain tractable when each market has at most three firms, and quintic demands remain tractable with at most two. These thresholds are exact: approximation at a fixed positive profit-regret tolerance is PPAD-hard for quartic demands with four firms per market, quintic demands with three, and sextic demands with two. Each hardness result uses one fixed demand curve in every market, a constant number of markets per firm, and globally nondecreasing strongly convex quadratic costs. We also give a polynomial-time algorithm for arbitrary-degree nonincreasing concave polynomial demands when each firm's convex polynomial cost depends only on its total production. The algorithm applies to arbitrary access graphs and permits firm-specific inverse demands. Its running time is polynomial in the input size and the logarithm of the inverse accuracy. The algorithm assigns one marginal charge to each firm and adjusts the charges until each firm's total sales approximate the quantity it would produce at that charge.

papers.title: A Weinstein manifold without any spherical Fukaya category
papers.abstract: We show that, after attaching a subcritical handle to $T^*\bP^2$ to obtain a manifold $M$, the integral wrapped Floer endomorphism algebra of a cotangent fibre admits no spherical refinement for any choice of brane structure; this obstructs the existence of any wrapped Fukaya category for $M$ over the sphere spectrum. We further discuss some features of the resulting Weinstein eight-manifold $M$, which is homotopy equivalent to $S^4$.

papers.title: Improving External Prediction in New Clusters with Mixed-Effects Models: Implications for Multicenter Studies
papers.abstract: Prediction models developed from multicenter data are often applied to new centers. A linear mixed model (LMM) captures between-center heterogeneity through random effects. However, a new center's random effect is unknown, so the LMM predicts from fixed effects alone, as does a standard linear model (LM) that ignores clustering. The two models thus differ only in how fixed effects are estimated, and it is unclear whether the LMM predicts better. We decompose the prediction error in a new center into fixed-effect estimation error, between-center variation, and residual variation. Because the last two components are identical for both models, any LMM advantage must come from more precise fixed-effect estimates. In simulations across diverse designs and random-effect structures, the LMM generally achieved lower mean squared error than the LM. Relative gains increased with the number of predictors, between-center heterogeneity, and imbalance in center sizes, and decreased as training data grew. Modeling a random slope yielded additional gains that increased with between-center variation in the predictor effect. In a stress test using held-out eICU hospitals selected for strong outcome heterogeneity, a random-intercept LMM predicted ICU length of stay more accurately than an LM. These findings clarify the conditions under which mixed models can improve prediction in new centers and can inform model development for multicenter studies.

papers.title: Residual Allan Stability under Periodic Auxiliary Ramsey Sampling
papers.abstract: The timing of auxiliary Ramsey measurements can change the frequency stability associated with a drifting pulse shift at a fixed nominal Fisher-information rate for a constant shift. For periodic instantaneous observations of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck shift with causal prediction between updates, we derive the exact residual covariance averaged over the update cycle and the corresponding Allan variance at arbitrary averaging times. Relative to a continuous Kalman reference at the same information rate, periodic estimation increases the cycle-averaged estimation-error variance, reduces the short-time residual Allan variance, and increases its long-time value. Its covariance decays more slowly at the origin and has a larger integral. We extend the result to instantaneous sensing of the sum of finitely many independent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck modes. Integrated observations preserve the short-time ordering for the scalar shift, and numerical calculations resolve the dependence of the crossover on window duration. A zero-order-hold comparison shows that the short-time ordering can change when the same estimator drives a different correction command. A three-level Ramsey model of coherent population trapping (CPT) maps the discriminator response to an effective information budget and illustrates how the dark times affect the choice of schedule.

papers.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
papers.abstract: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented. In this work, we focus on the organizations that make up the AI supply chain: the complex network of actors that contribute to the development and deployment of AI. We motivate the examination of the organizational AI supply chain---highlighting concerns about concentration, power, chokepoints, cascading failures, fragmented accountability, and risk---then describe our pipeline for mapping the AI supply chain. Our pipeline yields our main contribution: a multilayered, large-scale dataset of actors and relationships in the AI ecosystem, annotated with dates, descriptions, types, tags, and more. This work takes a step toward systematically mapping and measuring the AI supply chain and its properties, cataloging how models, data, chips, infrastructure, capital, and even talent flow between organizations. This data enable critical examinations of industry relationships and yield insights into the political economy of AI development and concentration. We provide several illustrative analyses, including studying the most central actors, analyzing network concentration, and identifying communities and chokepoints. While our dataset is fairly comprehensive, it is also necessarily incomplete: public documents omit private deals, and coverage is shaped by search design. Together, the approach, data, and findings aim to serve as a resource for studying the AI ecosystem. The dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/sarahcen/ai-supply-chain and can be explored interactively at https://aisupplychains.org/.

papers.title: Render the Robot, Generate the World: One Video World Model Across Embodiments
papers.abstract: Predicting the consequences of an agent's actions requires modeling both the body's motion and the environment's response. Most video world models attempt to learn both from numerical actions, even though geometry and kinematics already specify the intended motion. We introduce Doppel, an embodiment-agnostic video world model conditioned on camera-aligned renderings of future body configurations and numerical action trajectories. By explicitly providing the intended motion, Doppel can focus on predicting object motion and interaction-driven changes in the environment. Rendered motion also provides a common visual interface across different embodiments and action spaces. To train on robot datasets without camera extrinsics, we recover camera poses and align rendered trajectories with recorded observations. We jointly train a single shared video backbone and conditioning adapter on eight datasets spanning eight robot and human embodiments, from single- and bimanual robot arms to a dexterous humanoid and human hands and bodies, using about 600 hours of video without embodiment labels. Across three robot-arm datasets, Doppel improves PSNR over action-only baselines by 1.00 dB on held-out trajectories and 1.20 dB under out-of-distribution evaluation, while predicting more consistent object motion. Training on all eight embodiments (Doppel-8) improves robot predictions over the three-robot model (Doppel-3) on four of six evaluation sets. Project page: https://doppelwm.github.io/.

papers.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
papers.abstract: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima. We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution. The loop consists of three steps: (1) User-driven evaluation lets simulated users raise their requirements as issues while they work with the harness over multiple turns. (2) Team-based modification implements those requirements as generalizable changes rather than task-specific patches. (3) Requirement-driven selection merges a change only when it resolves a verified requirement and passes review. Empirically, on held-out tasks, AHE-Beta raises pass@1 from 21.9% to 33.3% while using 40.8% fewer tokens than Base Harness, and achieves higher pass@1 than Claude Code, Meta-Harness, and AHE. In a blind human A/B test, real users prefer AHE-Beta in 31 of 48 valid pairs and rate it higher on all five dimensions, matching the directional preference of the user simulator. The human A/B results show that AHE-Beta achieves its goal of aligning harness evolution with real-world user requirements. Without further evolution, the gains transfer to GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with pass@1 improvements of 15.8% and 5.3% over Base Harness. Together, these results show that requirement-centered harness evolution is a more general method for improving agent capabilities.

papers.title: Unique determination of ellipsoids by their intrinsic volumes
papers.abstract: We prove that ellipsoids in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge 2$, are uniquely determined by their intrinsic volumes up to congruence, resolving the conjecture posed by Gusakova and Zaporozhets in 2017.

papers.title: The Holomorphic Reduction of Pseudoconvex Homogeneous Manifolds
papers.abstract: Suppose $G$ is a connected complex Lie group and $H$ is a closed complex subgroup. Then there exists a closed complex subgroup $J$ of $G$ containing $H$ such that the fibration $π:G/H \to G/J$ is the holomorphic reduction of $G/H$, i.e., $G/J$ is holomorphically separable and ${\mathcal O}(G/H) \cong π^*{\mathcal O}(G/J)$. In this paper we prove that if $G/H$ is pseudoconvex, i.e., if $G/H$ admits a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion function, then $G/J$ is Stein and $J/H$ has no non-constant holomorphic functions.

papers.title: Strong Epsilon-Near-Zero Confinement and Interface-Controlled Dynamics in Inverse-Designed Transparent Conducting Oxide Cavities
papers.abstract: Achieving optical modulation that is both strong and ultrafast remains a central challenge in time-varying photonics. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that combining inverse-designed cavities that utilize transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) operating at the epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) point with boundaries that support carrier transport can meet this requirement. This is achieved by leveraging ENZ-enhanced optical absorption and electron heating with interface-engineered carrier relaxation. A multilayer inverse-design framework, combined with a structural disorder-aware correction loop, is developed to preserve robust resonant absorption in ultrathin TCO films under realistic material disorder. Relative to conventional TCO cavity geometries, the inverse-designed structures exhibit stronger light confinement, greater electron temperature modulation, and markedly faster recovery. Beyond cavity design, interfacial barrier engineering and adjacent-layer doping emerge as effective degrees of freedom for co-designing spectral and temporal dynamics. Furthermore, our theoretical framework shows that the inverse-designed cavity supports richer oscillatory transmittance dynamics on the few-optical-cycle timescale compared to its single-film counterpart, with interfacial control enabling further temporal compression. The combined control of optical confinement and interfacial dynamics establishes inverse-designed TCO cavities as a viable platform for time-varying photonic media capable of supporting strong and ultrafast optical responses.

papers.title: The Optimal Competitive Ratio for Subadditive Online Combinatorial Auctions is Less Than 1/2
papers.abstract: We construct a four-buyer online combinatorial auction with independent subadditive valuations and a fixed, known arrival order in which every online rule earns strictly less than $1/2$ of the expected offline optimum. A common partition, revealed at the third arrival, gives the first three buyers one unit of welfare per item. If the rule uses three distinct partitions, either an item allocated early contributes zero or the fourth buyer's expected value for the remaining bundle is one less than its size. We compute the optimal online and offline welfare exactly and show that a $1/2$ guarantee always holds with at most three buyers.

papers.title: Zero-Temperature Energetics of a First-Order Surface Phase Transition from Diffraction
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions are governed by the balance between zero-temperature energy, thermal vibrational energy, and entropy, yet these contributions are rarely accessible experimentally. Here, we establish a diffraction-based route to determine them for the prototypical Si(111)-In atomic-wire system. From the temperature-dependent Debye-Waller attenuation of reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) intensities we extract distinct Debye temperatures for the low-temperature $(8{\times}2)$ ground state and the high-temperature $(4{\times}1)$ phase. The softer vibrational spectrum of the high-temperature phase yields the entropy gain that stabilizes this phase above the critical temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$. Evaluating the thermodynamic balance between internal energy and entropy at $T_\mathrm{c} = 125\,\mathrm{K}$ yields a zero-temperature energy difference of $ΔE_0 = 138\,\mathrm{meV}/(8{\times}2)$, including the difference in vibrational zero-point energies of the two phases, thus providing direct access to hidden thermodynamic parameters of a first-order surface phase transition.

papers.title: Hardness of "Infinite Energy" Puzzles
papers.abstract: Infinite Energy (by Light Potato, 2025) is a single-player puzzle in which one wires a network of sockets so that, after every power source is unplugged, energy keeps circulating and leaves every board energized. We study several variants of the game and the complexity of deciding whether an instance can be won. The variants can be played at https://infinite-energy-peer-review.netlify.app, which also has worked examples of the reduction techniques. The colorless game, with connectability given by an arbitrary matrix, is NP-hard (by reduction from Hamiltonian Path) and lies in PSPACE. We give a seven-socket instance winnable only by charging a temporary battery loop and then breaking it, so the natural "charge and keep" strategy fails. We reduce NP-membership to one conjecture: that every winnable instance has a winning play in which no socket is charged twice. Two variants bound the complexity more tightly. The unconstrained variant, in which connectability is unrestricted, is $\mathsf{TC}^0$-complete under $\mathsf{AC}^0$ Turing reductions (hence in L). The geometric variant, in which connectability is set by proximity of points in $\mathbb{R}^k$, stays NP-hard for every fixed $k \ge 2$ via reduction from Hamiltonian Path over grid graphs. The one-dimensional case is open. The colored variant is NP-hard, though a matching upper bound remains open.

papers.title: Locally infrared finite two-loop amplitudes for multi Higgs production in association with one jet
papers.abstract: We study the two-loop amplitudes for multi-Higgs production through a massive top-quark loop in association with one jet. We consider the quark-antiquark channel with a final-state gluon, $q\bar q\to g+nH$ although our construction applies to crossed channel as well. We utilize (non-local in momentum space) Ward identities to factorize longitudinal and gauge degrees of freedom through exact identities between Feynman graphs without reference to an infrared region. In the genuine two loop topologies, we replace the internal gluons by their physical degrees of freedom and show that the resulting amplitude is free of collinear singularities. The only remaining infrared divergence is a soft singularity that can be identified with a change of reference gauge vector. We construct explicit soft counterterms for these singularities, obtaining a locally infrared-finite representation. We verify that the factorized longitudinal degrees of freedom reproduce the remaining infrared poles of the original Feynman graphs. Our formalism requires no counter-terms for collinear finiteness or for manifesting Ward identities in various regions since we perform a decomposition of covariant gauge Feynman graphs. We expect its extension to more complicated processes to eliminate all collinear singularities--particularly in the initial state.

papers.title: PrismRestore: A Compact Restoration Toolbox for Agentic Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Agentic image restoration composes operations to handle mixed degradations, yet its toolbox often requires storing multiple restoration networks. We propose PrismRestore, which constructs a compact bank of callable restoration actions from a single frozen all-in-one model. Our approach builds on task-dependent yet overlapping channel responses in the shared model. An offline task-prior search uses activation and gradient statistics to group channels with similar response profiles, then searches task-specific modulation coefficients over non-representative channels while leaving representative channels unmodulated. The resulting prior bank enables explicit action selection and composition without additional restoration backbones or task-specific adapter modules. A state-conditioned policy learns to compose these actions using Group Relative Policy Optimization. Its objective separately normalizes fidelity and perceptual feedback within groups of trajectories sampled for the same input, and combines terminal evaluation with return-to-go derived from stepwise quality changes. Experiments on synthetic composite-degradation and real-world multi-task benchmarks show improvements over the evaluated all-in-one baselines and restoration quality competitive with multi-model agents. PrismRestore achieves these results with a single restoration backbone and faster inference than the evaluated agentic baselines.

papers.title: The role of externally-driven density fluctuations in the enhancement of beam spray
papers.abstract: Speckled laser beams, commonly used to ionize and heat plasma for inertial confinement fusion and high-energy-density experiments, are shown to drive long-wavelength plasma-density fluctuations that induce beam spray in other laser beams. Experiments show that a 1053 nm beam undergoes increased beam spray when 351 nm speckled heater beams are on. These observations indicate that the high-intensity speckles sustain an increased level of steady-state density fluctuations. Modeling of these fluctuations predicts amplitudes that are orders of magnitude larger than the level of thermal fluctuations. Beam propagation simulations show increased beam spray due to self-focusing and filamentation when heater-driven density fluctuations are included.

papers.title: Stock bubbles in limited participation models with power utilities
papers.abstract: We prove that the equilibrium state-price deflated cum-dividend stock-price process in Guasoni, Larsen, and Leoni (2025) is a strict local martingale. Our result is based on proving that the unrestricted trader faces an endogenously complete model.

papers.title: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Second-order Error Bound
papers.abstract: An effective theory of open quantum systems should preserve the detailed balance structure inherited from microscopic reversibility and remain accurate throughout relaxation. Meeting both requirements is particularly challenging in quantum many-body systems, where dense spectra can invalidate the secular approximation even at weak coupling. Here we construct a nonsecular quantum master equation that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (TR-KMS) detailed balance. Under suitable conditions, we prove a time-uniform $O(λ^2)$ bound on the difference between the predicted and exact reduced density matrices, where $λ$ is the system-bath coupling strength. Our construction completes the Redfield generator by imposing detailed balance while matching its dissipative and coherent coefficients at resonance. In this approach, TR-KMS detailed balance is compatible with resonance matching, whereas its counterpart without time reversal is not. In a benchmark against the exact microscopic dynamics of two coupled oscillators, our equation maintains $O(λ^2)$ accuracy across secular and nonsecular regimes, outperforming the existing detailed-balance equations tested. These results provide a systematic route from microscopic models to thermodynamically consistent descriptions of open quantum dynamics beyond the secular approximation.

papers.title: Dressed-State Quantum Information Processing Using a Multilayer Ion Trap Chip with an Integrated Radio Frequency Resonator
papers.abstract: We present the experimental preparation of a radio frequency (RF)-dressed-state qubit, the coherent operation of a single RF-dressed qubit, and the selective readout of RF-dressed hyperfine states of $^{171}$Yb${^+}$ ions trapped using a novel microstructured ion trap chip. We demonstrate the individual addressing of RF-dressed-state qubits in a two-ion Coulomb crystal. To this end, we developed, manufactured, and characterized a trap chip specifcally designed for quantum information processing with RF-dressed-state qubits. The chip consists of multiple layers, one of which includes an integrated resonator that creates a gradient of the RF magnetic field amplitude along the axis of a linear ion crystal. This RF gradient enables the individual addressing of dressed qubit states as well as their coupling. We characterize the ion trap chip experimentally using the hyperfine states of the electronic ground state of laser cooled $^{171}$Yb${^+}$ ions and by applying a single, global, modulated RF field oscillating near 12.6 GHz that drives dressed-state resonances. We present a microfabricated multilayer ion trap chip specifically designed for quantum information processing based on dressed-state qubits. This ion trap chip consists of multiple layers, one of which includes an integrated radio frequency (RF) resonator, creating a gradient of the RF magnetic field amplitude that allows for individual qubit addressing and qubit-qubit coupling. We experimentally characterize this ion trap chip demonstrating dressed-qubit state preparation, coherent single dressed-qubit operation, and dressed-state-selective read-out using hyperfine states of the electronic ground state of $^{171}$Yb${^+}$. For this purpose, a global modulated RF driving field oscillating near 12.6 GHz is applied to the ions. In addition, we demonstrate individual addressing of dressed-state qubits in a two-ion Coulomb crystal.

papers.title: Prediction and Screening of $η$-carbide-type Nitrides for Ammonia Synthesis
papers.abstract: Synthesis of ammonia is of critical importance to applications in energy, industrial chemistry, and especially agriculture, and is accomplished industrially using the carbon- and energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. η-carbide-type nitrides such as Co3Mo3N have gained attention in recent years as alternative ammonia synthesis catalysts with the potential to lower these energy demands. Co3Mo3N is experimentally observed to undergo a reversible phase transition from Co3Mo3N to Co6Mo6N, offering a chemical looping-based NH3 synthesis route that has not been fully explored. In this work, we present a first-principles exploration of phase change in the Co3Mo3N/Co6Mo6N system as a prototype η-carbide-type nitride and fit a cluster expansion to predict the energy of Co3Mo3Nx systems. We use our results to identify the phase energy difference as a useful screening criterion for the phase change process. We then apply this methodology to screen a broad range of η-carbide-type nitrides that combine group 4-6 transition metals with Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, or Zn. We report strong periodic trends in phase energy difference, which increases with decreasing period and group number of the group 4-6 transition metal and with distance from group 9 for the other metal. We identify Co3W3N, Fe3W3N, and several quaternary nitrides as promising candidates for NH3 synthesis via a phase change mechanism.

papers.title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
papers.abstract: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization. We decompose the first-layer weights into a signal component aligned with the teacher and an orthogonal complement, and analyze their joint SGD dynamics together with the second layer in the proportional limit. We show that although SGD updates to the complement are initially isotropic, the training dynamics induce teacher-dependent spectral spikes in the complement Gram matrix. This emergent anisotropy provides a concrete mechanism by which representation variance is amplified, and generalization degrades. To isolate this effect, we introduce Decomposed Dynamics, an analytically tractable surrogate whose asymptotic test-error dynamics coincide with those of SGD. In simulations with a ReLU student, freezing the directions of the orthogonal complement improves generalization relative to training them. Finally, we show that the signal component rapidly aligns with the second-layer weights, revealing strong cross-layer coupling even in this shallow setting. Together, our results provide a dynamical explanation for how feature learning outside the teacher subspace harms generalization.

papers.title: Shadowing Property for Linear Operators on Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: This note is dedicated to the study of the shadowing property for (bounded linear) operators on Banach spaces. We combine the spectral characterization of the shadowing property, recently established by Dragičević and Pituk, with tools from local spectral theory, to obtain new results and simpler proofs of known results on shadowing for operators. We also prove that the shadowing property always implies the average shadowing property and the asymptotic average shadowing property for invertible operators on Banach spaces. Furthermore, we investigate the shadowing property for some specific classes of operators, such as weighted composition operators and adjoints of multiplication operators on certain spaces of holomorphic functions.

papers.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square torus
papers.abstract: For each $1<s<2$ we construct a solution of the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square two-torus with initial data in $H^s$ whose $H^s$ norm tends to infinity as $t\to+\infty$. The growth can be arbitrarily slow. More precisely, the squared norm agrees, up to a bounded error at all positive times, with the number of selected axial frequencies $K_j$ for which $K_j^s\le t$. The central construction couples a finite tree of orthogonal frequency pairs to a periodic one-dimensional solution of the same equation. Each transfer leaves a nonvanishing Fourier coefficient on the horizontal axis. Control on an entire half-line allows successive transfers to retain the coefficients produced earlier.

papers.title: Batch-Dynamic Coreness and Applications with Logarithmic Work via Balanced Pressures
papers.abstract: We give a parallel algorithm that maintains a one-sided $(2+\varepsilon)$-approximation of all core numbers under batches of edge insertions and deletions. For fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the expected amortized work is $O(\log n)$ per edge update, and each batch has deterministic polylogarithmic depth. This improves on the previously known $(4+\varepsilon)$-approximation and $O(\log^2 n)$ amortized work bounds. This approximation factor approaches the factor-two limit for polylogarithmic update and query time under the OMv conjecture. Our algorithm is based on assigning each vertex a "pressure" and splits each edge's unit load smoothly between its endpoints according to their pressures. After each batch of updates, our dynamic algorithm adjusts the pressures of vertices in parallel to restore balance between the pressures and loads. We show that by maintaining balanced pressures we can obtain good approximations of core numbers. Our construction also gives a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation of the densest-subgraph value with logarithmic expected amortized work and supports batch-dynamic maximal matching, clique counting, forest decomposition, and coloring in low-arboricity graphs with improved or matching work bounds. We give a practical implementation of our batch-dynamic coreness algorithm and find that it is able to achieve smaller empirical error than the state-of-the-art parallel batch-dynamic implementation, while running faster. On six real-world graphs, it runs $32\times$ faster than that implementation in geometric mean and $4.1\times$ faster than a state-of-the-art heuristic baseline. On three graphs with up to 1.8 billion edges, it is $9.2\times$ faster than the heuristic baseline.

papers.title: ShadowTransfer: A Geographic Transfer Benchmark for Overhead Shadow Detection
papers.abstract: Overhead aerial imagery feeds dense-prediction pipelines that are routinely trained in one geographic region and deployed in another, yet no benchmark measures how shadow detection models transfer across regions. Existing overhead shadow datasets either lack a geographic transfer protocol or rely on automatically generated labels. We introduce ShadowTransfer, a benchmark of 4,500 human-verified shadow masks across three U.S. cities at two native resolutions, paired with a leave-one-city-out evaluation protocol. Under vanilla training, holding out the test city costs 3.5 to 7.8 mIoU across four architectures, the gap remains significant when the training set grows from 225 to 900 images, and six of eight adaptation methods degrade more than vanilla training on average. We propose a three-probe framework that diagnoses where and how the transfer breaks: the failure operates in feature space, beyond the reach of pixel-histogram matching, shows up as a confidence collapse on shadow pixels while background confidence stays intact, and is recoverable by retraining different architectural components depending on the model: encoder for some, decoder for others. These findings replicate on INRIA building footprints, suggesting they describe geographic transfer beyond shadows. Guided by the diagnosis, we build Spectral Information Bottleneck (SIB), a plug-in module with one component per finding. Across the 9 (architecture, held-out city) cells, SIB has the smallest mean gap to the within-city upper bound of the ten methods we evaluate (6.42 mIoU), level with FDA. The benchmark, LOCO protocol, code, and trained models are released to support reproducible evaluation of geographic transfer in overhead dense prediction.

papers.title: A Geometric Calderón Problem for Differential Forms
papers.abstract: We establish boundary determination and global partial-data uniqueness for Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential $p$-forms. We derive an explicit recursion for its full symbol and determine the full boundary jet of the metric, modulo conformal gauge in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$. For $p\geq1$, partial data determine metrics that are analytic in the interior and near the measured boundary subset, up to isometry or conformal equivalence. The global uniqueness relies on a new projection-kernel embedding that detects the unobserved boundary through rank loss and small eigenvalues. We also establish global partial-data uniqueness for smooth metrics with harmonic curvature, using elliptic-transport unique continuation and, in the critical dimension, conformal-geodesic coordinates. A Weyl nondegeneracy condition further upgrades conformal equivalence to isometry.

papers.title: Mine Locally, Verify Globally: Exact Recovery, Compilation, and Distortion of Mined Temporal Rules
papers.abstract: Specification mining extracts temporal rules that describe relationships between events in recorded system traces. Applying these rules in distributed monitoring systems is more difficult because observations come from different nodes, whose clocks may not be synchronized, and events may be lost or reordered during transmission. In this paper, we study how to aggregate the coverage of mined rules across observers, determine whether their temporal windows are needed during monitoring, and characterize their detection under event loss. Our evaluation uses IPv6 packet traces collected from 21 receivers across four continents. We show that local mining followed by global confirmation recovers centralized rule coverage under suitable conditions while substantially reducing communication overhead. In contrast, merging traces with unaligned clocks can distort coverage by introducing incorrect temporal matches. A window-gain criterion identifies rules that require temporal state, while our loss analysis and broker experiments demonstrate why contiguous losses can be more damaging than independent losses. The results identify separate requirements for aggregating observations, selecting monitor state, and handling event loss.

papers.title: Toward high-throughput, low-latency structural biology using light, Part I: Protein-ligand pose determination
papers.abstract: We demonstrate for the first time that an optical spectroscopy - electron-vibration-vibration two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy (EVV 2DIR) - has sufficient structural competence to enable the reconstruction of the three-dimensional geometries of drug-protein binding at the level needed for practical drug discovery applications. Klug et al. previously demonstrated experimental detection of drug binding to a kinase using EVV 2DIR. Here we use a quantum mechanical approach to calculate and assign elements of EVV 2DIR spectra for the spectral region 1200-1800 cm$^{-1}$ / 1100-1800 cm$^{-1}$ of 92 protein-ligand complexes. This dataset includes ligand-target poses drawn from existing crystal structures and ligand-target poses created by docking and cofolding models. We find that binding-dependent spectral features are robust, interpretable, and consistent across poses in a given binding mode, and distinct for each unique hydrogen bonding geometry. We construct a spectral distance metric to distinguish poses that conform to the ligand-target hydrogen-bonding pattern of the crystal structure from those that do not. These results show that, given a set of predicted ligand-target poses containing the correct geometry, the hydrogen-bonding pattern of the valid pose may be rapidly identified by comparing simulated and experimental EVV 2DIR spectra. Finally, we discuss the practical implications for a new, high throughput structural biology for drug discovery that will be the subject of forthcoming manuscripts, noting that the base technologies to perform EVV 2DIR quickly and efficiently already exist and will enable a novel structure to be determined in only minutes for each sample. Moreover, this can be achieved without the need for crystallization, isotopic labeling, or low temperatures, non-destructively using picogram quantities of material.

papers.title: New Observational Insights into Generalised Axion-Like Dark Energy
papers.abstract: We consider a quintessence model based on a generalised axion-like scalar field potential, originally introduced as a phenomenological framework to describe the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe. The model exhibits a tracking regime that alleviates the coincidence problem and naturally leads to a phase of late-time acceleration driven by an effective cosmological constant, without requiring fine-tuning of the scalar field initial conditions. In this work, we confront the background cosmological evolution of this model with current observations by performing a parameter inference analysis using cosmic microwave background distance priors, baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, Type Ia supernovae, the SH0ES distance ladder, cosmic chronometers, and gamma-ray bursts. This analysis allows us to assess the observational viability of the model, its ability to reconcile different cosmological datasets, and its statistical performance relative to $Λ$CDM.

papers.title: "I Don't Think It's a Scam": A First Look at Family Intervention Barriers in Elder Abuse Discussions on Reddit and Baidu Tieba
papers.abstract: When older adults trust scammers despite warnings, families face obstacles to intervention. Complainants aged 60 and older reported \$4.9 billion in losses in 2024 to the U.S. Internet Crime Complaint Center. To investigate family intervention barriers to elder scams, we collected 2M Reddit posts from May 2021 to June 2026 and 2B Baidu Tieba posts from 2007 to 2026. The final corpora contain 13,082 Reddit posts and 3,933 Baidu Tieba posts, labeled using platform-specific codebooks, manual reference annotations, and LLM coding. Through a mixed-methods analysis, we find that scams often extend beyond a single incident and are reported alongside debt problems and broken family relationships. In 68.0\% of Reddit posts recording reactions, older adults showed resistance or continued involvement; in Baidu Tieba family-confrontation posts, 41.9\% showed continued belief. Relatives identified fraud in 74.4\% of Reddit posts and narrated cases on Baidu Tieba, but without the victim's consent, relatives may lack the legal authority to intervene. In Reddit posts recording reactions, account locks or credential changes appeared in 8.9\% under resistance or continued involvement, compared with 33.3\% under acceptance. Measures such as phone or network monitoring and financial takeover were reported more often under resistance. Recovering funds is very limited in posts recording follow-up results of fraud; Baidu Tieba users reported that police classified older adults' voluntary transfers as civil disputes.

papers.title: When Time-Reversible Sensor Records Require Hidden Dissipation
papers.abstract: A binary sensor record can be time reversible yet require dissipation in every compatible finite-state Markov model. For a four-state sensor with correlated dwell times, two observed switching statistics give an exact equilibrium criterion and, when equilibrium is excluded, a positive lower bound on entropy production independent of hidden-state number. An explicit four-state construction provides an upper bound on the minimum dissipation. For a noisy Poisson sensor, the bounds differ by less than a factor of two and vanish at a kinetic matching point while the sensor remains dissipative.

papers.title: Beyond hidden zeros and uniqueness in Tr$(ϕ^3)$: Block and rod zeros in any Tr$(ϕ^m)$
papers.abstract: Hidden zeros have proven powerful tools for reconstructing amplitudes in Tr$(ϕ^3)$, a theory of colored scalars with cubic interactions. We show that these structures extend to any Tr$(ϕ^m)$ theory. For odd $m$, we construct \emph{block zeros} from orthogonal sums of consecutive momenta, generalizing the original cubic hidden zeros. For every $m\geq4$, including even $m$, we describe a second family of nonlinear \emph{rod zeros} through a rod packing problem. In Tr$(ϕ^4)$ this construction reduces to a simple rank-one condition on a matrix of momentum contractions. We connect this new zero to the classic threshold nullification zeros of Voloshin, where certain amplitudes in massive $ϕ^4$ theory vanish when all produced particles are at rest. Finally, we demonstrate the reconstruction power of these zeros. Assuming locality, we prove that the rod zeros uniquely fix all Tr$(ϕ^m)$ tree amplitudes for $m\geq4$ up to normalization. We also conjecture that the block zeros enforce both locality and unitarity for any Tr$(ϕ^m)$ theory with odd $m$.

papers.title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators
papers.abstract: We present a general framework for modeling and learning equivariant functions between finite dimensional semisimple real group representations, unifying constructions developed across many application areas. Our model is a linear combination of equivariant polynomial features whose coefficients are arbitrary learnable functions of invariant polynomial features. We take as features minimal homogeneous generators for the invariant algebra and the covariant module over the invariant algebra, up to prescribed degrees. We provide a Python package that automatically computes these features and fits the resulting models to training data. The algorithm for feature computation requires explicit isotypic decompositions of the input and output representations, along with explicit Clebsch-Gordan decompositions of the tensor product of irreducible representations, and achieves speedups over alternative methods in computational algebra. Numerical experiments in scientific modeling demonstrate the full learning pipeline and yield accurate predictors with few trainable parameters, using the model both for end-to-end prediction and within layers of larger architectures.

papers.title: Efficient search for microlensed gravitational-wave signals with matched filtering and a two-image statistic
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences can be microlensed by compact objects along the line of sight, producing frequency-dependent waveform distortions. As standard matched-filter searches rely on unlensed templates without accounting for lensing effects, microlensed signals can lose signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) through template mismatch and suffer further losses from signal-consistency tests. We quantify both effects for the $\texttt{PyCBC}$ search using microlensed injections in simulated data. The two losses occupy different regions of lens parameter space in the geometric optics representation: template mismatch is governed by the relative magnification of the two images, while the consistency-test penalty is governed by their time delay. We show that a microlensed signal lies in the two-dimensional subspace spanned by a template and its time-shifted copy, allowing the relative magnification and Morse phase to be maximized over analytically, leaving only the time delay to search. The resulting statistic requires no extension of the template bank and reduces the median loss in re-weighted SNR from $10\%$ to $1.6\%$, and the $90^\mathrm{th}$ percentile from $41\%$ to $9\%$. At a false-alarm rate of one per day, the relative detection volume improves by about $6\%$ across all injections, and by a factor of $1.9$ for the $10\%$ of injections most affected by lensing. In addition to increased detection capacities, we also show how the detection statistic can be used to establish the lensed nature of the trigger. Therefore, the work proposed here lays the foundation for an effective search and identification of microlensed signals in gravitational-wave data.

papers.title: ProvCards: Artifact-Oriented Provenance for Heterogeneous Scientific Workflows
papers.abstract: Reproducibility in scientific workflows is hindered by heterogeneous components and execution environments, as well as fragmented provenance capture. Although existing approaches offer established semantics and workflow-specific solutions, provenance remains difficult to capture, exchange, and compose across workflow boundaries. We present ProvCards, an artifact-oriented approach that treats provenance as a first-class artifact grounded in the W3C PROV Data Model. Individual workflow components can generate cards that are stored, exchanged, reused, and composed independently of any workflow system or centralized execution context. ProvDecks group related cards into portable scopes while preserving their identities. ProvGraphs provide derived views for provenance reconstruction, querying, visualization, and analysis. Together, these representations support coherent, task-specific provenance views across heterogeneous components, facilitating traceability, reuse, and reproducibility. We implement ProvCards using a graph-based infrastructure and evaluate them in a scientific data-processing workflow. The results demonstrate independent provenance capture at the component level, composition across component boundaries, and reconstruction for querying and analysis. ProvCards provide a portable, composable, and incrementally extensible foundation for provenance management in heterogeneous scientific workflows.

papers.title: AMISS: An Integrity Framework for Magnetic Navigation
papers.abstract: Magnetic Navigation (MagNav) is a promising alternative to traditional systems like Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), offering resistance to jamming or spoofing attacks to which the latter are vulnerable. MagNav matches scalar magnetic measurements over time against a known map of Earth's magnetic anomaly in order to position a vehicle. MagNav is therefore sensitive to the quality of these maps, especially to errors in the survey data that the maps are derived from. In order to be a reliable and mature navigation technology, MagNav must satisfy integrity requirements for mitigation of such faults. To this end, a solution-separation monitoring algorithm is developed that performs a role equivalent to Advanced Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (ARAIM) in GNSS, which detects faults as well as generates worst-case bounds (protection levels) on estimation error for faults too small to be detected. It is shown how these integrity methods can be developed in a \emph{windowed-in-time} sense, where subsets of measurements over a time window are compared with each other in order to detect outliers that can potentially result from errors in the map. The applicability of the approach is demonstrated using results obtained using synthetic aircraft data with injected faults.

papers.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
papers.abstract: User simulators offer a scalable way to evaluate interactive agents, but how to assess their quality remains underexplored. In particular, it is unclear whether existing user simulator evaluation frameworks reliably detect meaningful failures in simulated user behavior. This uncertainty makes it difficult to interpret simulator evaluation. To understand what a high benchmark score tells us about simulator quality, we (meta-)evaluate the metrics themselves. To instantiate this meta-evaluation, we deliberately perturb simulated replays to induce failures such as altered goals, omitted constraints, premature stopping, and acceptance of broken work, then test whether the metrics penalize these failures. Evaluation methods from three prior studies detect only 5-6 of the 10 perturbations; their combined scores even favor populations instructed to accept broken work over unmodified controls. Motivated by these gaps, we propose a new evaluation suite that combines utility of user simulators for evaluating agents and two measures of fidelity to real users: population-level fidelity assesses collective interaction patterns, while trace-level fidelity assesses the preservation of individual users' goals, constraints, and persona. Under the same detection criterion, our evaluation suite detects all 10 perturbations. Evaluating six user simulators on 351 real multi-turn sessions in which 348 distinct users across 23 languages and agents work together to create and refine artifacts such as full-stack web apps, games, design assets, and automated workflows, we find that population-level measures can miss when a simulated user pursues the wrong goal, ignores a constraint, or behaves out of character, highlighting the need to assess fidelity at comprehensive granularities.

papers.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
papers.abstract: A fixed dispatch rate for LLM inference becomes stale as serving fleets resize and request sizes change. Generative output length is unknown at admission, and shared provider pools can lose capacity. We present Cap-and-Track, a design for asynchronous inference across provider capacity and internal GPUs. Meta's traffic shaper implements Cap-and-Track for post and live-video understanding. Refusals signal the backend's current admission ceiling. Durable priority queues hold excess work outside execution, including refused requests for retry. Cap is a fail-fast admission check at the saturated resource that refuses work before a long wait. Using only those refusals, the Track dispatcher probes upward and backs off. It follows the ceiling without output-length prediction or a fleet-level rate to retune. In a concurrent same-traffic production A/B, the shaper ran per-replica Cap plus Track. It served a classifier on 43% fewer H100s than its queued, fixed-rate precursor, though lower-priority work waited longer at backfill peaks. In steady-capacity real-engine replay, Track ran within 1% of the goodput of a fixed rate tuned above measured capacity, with about a quarter of that rate's refusal share. The shaper carries more than 300 million online requests and hundreds of terabytes of media a day. During a backfill, it handled 1.1 billion requests in its busiest 24 hours. Lessons include keeping queues inside inference engines just long enough to fill batches, steering dispatch by capacity refusals alone, keeping dispatch stateful, and sizing fleets by how long low-priority work can wait.

papers.title: Residual-Algebraic Design of Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Symmetry-preserving (SP) variational quantum circuits restrict evolution to physically relevant sectors of Hilbert space, but symmetry preservation alone does not guarantee accessibility within those sectors. We show that a restricted generator set can possess a residual dynamical Lie algebra whose commutant further decomposes the target symmetry sector into invariant blocks. The associated block populations are conserved and impose a kinematic upper bound on the fidelity with a target state. We then invert this diagnostic into a circuit-design principle: candidate SP generators can be screened before variational optimization by asking whether they break the residual commutant, which invariant blocks they couple, and what adjoint module they generate under the residual algebra. For two orthogonal residual blocks we prove that a single elementary real inter-block rotation generates the full orthogonal algebra. We further derive a complex escape criterion: if the real and imaginary parts of an inter-block seed are independent over the residual intertwiner algebra, the generated module is the full complex coupling space and the enlarged algebra becomes special unitary. A connected residual-block graph yields a natural multi-block generalization and suggests minimum-cost spanning-tree circuit design. We demonstrate this design principle in the XXZ and Hubbard models, where residual-algebra screening identifies SP circuit extensions that remove the relevant accessibility obstructions. These examples establish a unified route from residual-symmetry diagnosis and fidelity bounds to predictive quantum circuit design.

papers.title: Improved Asymptotic Approximation Guarantees for Continuous-Review Lost-Sales and Dual-Sourcing Inventory Models
papers.abstract: We study continuous-review inventory models with unit Poisson demand and deterministic lead times: single sourcing with lost sales and dual sourcing with backlogging. Xin [Operations Research. 70(1):111--128 (2022)] establishes an asymptotic approximation factor of 1.79 for each model in its proportional-growth regime. Under the same assumptions, we obtain a factor of 1.248977 for the better of base-stock and constant-order policies for lost sales and a factor of 1.599528 for the better of dual-index and tailored base-surge policies for dual sourcing. The benchmark is the optimal long-run average cost over all policies using only current and past information. For lost sales, lead time and the lost-sales penalty grow proportionally. For dual sourcing, the lead-time difference grows proportionally to the express premium, the extra unit cost of faster supply, while express lead time and backorder penalty remain fixed. For sufficiently large fixed backorder penalties, the dual-sourcing factor improves to 1.248977. The improvements follow from stronger lower bounds on the optimal cost. We retain intermediate constraints on mean inventory for lost sales and use events determined only by future demand to bound backlog costs for dual sourcing.

papers.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts. To demonstrate the framework, we design an LLM-based system that plays the game for one of the paper's authors, drawing on an autoethnographic dataset spanning ten years of personal digital communication. In a 20-person deception study, interrogators choose our system over the author's own friends in 7 of 10 rounds, and the author over our system in 13 of 20; neither rate is distinguishable from chance at this sample size. We consider design improvements, applications of personal AI agents, and implications for identity and privacy.

papers.title: Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation
papers.abstract: Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work. We introduce the Creative AI Researcher (CAR), an agentic framework combining literature grounding, iterative development and explicit conceptual operators. CAR constructs a semantic knowledge graph from retrieved literature and equips an ideation agent with graph-retrieval tools and four operators: bisociation, analogy, exploration and elaboration. Each operator call is checked against structural acceptance conditions and recorded, producing a trace of intermediate transformations and declared literature sources. We evaluate CAR with two language-model backbones across 40 LiveIdeaBench research topics and two execution benchmarks. CAR achieves significantly higher methodological novelty (MN) than single-shot prompting and The AI Scientist. Its methodological novelty does not differ significantly from the Research Ideation Agent, while its feasibility scores are higher on both backbones. With a shared experiment executor, CAR achieves the highest pairwise win rate among the evaluated AI methods on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena. In a ten-condition ablation study, MN point estimates favor CAR over one-step proposal on both backbones, but no MN contrast survives correction for multiple comparisons. The results do not establish a consistent quality benefit from explicit operators beyond free-form iteration. CAR makes the sequence of operations and declared literature sources inspectable, separating judged idea quality from procedural traceability.

papers.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
papers.abstract: Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit. Calibration updates can also change region suitability and trigger the rebuilding of calibration-dependent resource structures. We present CREST, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that evaluates circuit-region compatibility before routing. It encodes gate dependencies and logical-qubit interactions alongside each candidate region's connectivity and current calibration attributes; bidirectional cross-graph attention relates the two representations, while real-device execution outcomes supervise candidate ranking. The trained scorer is reused with updated calibration attributes. Evaluations on 324 circuits from seven datasets on TianYan-176 show that CREST improves mean measurement-distribution fidelity by 19.03% over the strongest baseline and achieves the highest mean fidelity on every dataset. Furthermore, using updated calibration attributes, the same trained model maintains the highest overall mean fidelity across six measurement dates without retraining. With a unified model of circuit-region compatibility, CREST improves execution fidelity across diverse workloads and sustains that advantage as hardware calibration changes.

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of First-Quantised Chemistry with a Sum-of-Squares Representation
papers.abstract: Calculating molecular energies is expected to be an important application of quantum computers, but the most efficient algorithms to achieve this typically have significant space requirements. Scaling quantum processors to thousands of logical qubits is a daunting engineering challenge, so developing algorithms that run with reduced qubit requirements is of particular importance. Moreover, most algorithms are benchmarked on active spaces with about as many orbitals as electrons, missing dynamical correlation which is necessary to describe real chemistry. Capturing this correlation requires several times more orbitals than electrons, even in compact atomic-orbital basis sets.
